H1840.derivation: From H1835 (Dan, “judge”) + H410 (El, God): “God is my judge.”
H1840.gloss: Daniel — God is my judge (1890: the prophet’s own name, not a title he takes).

danielHits.gloss: renamed Belteshazzar; the Hebrew name is not erased
the king still knows both names
the last word of the book is spoken to this name

otherKjv.gloss: listed with Noah and Job as a righteous man
Jesus cites “Daniel the prophet” as a reader of last things

H1840.why: The book’s name is already an argument: history is a courtroom. Empires are weighed, not merely described. When the court of 7:9–10 sits, the prophet’s own name has been waiting for that scene.

H2235.derivation: From H2232 zaraʿ (to sow): something sown — a vegetable raised from seed (only in the plural; variant zerōʿôn).
H2235.gloss: vegetables / pulse (1890: things sown, seeds, grains, vegetables).

danielHits.gloss: give us pulse to eat, and water to drink
took away the portion of their meat… and gave them pulse

otherKjv.gloss: every herb bearing seed… to you it shall be for meat
as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth

H2235.why: Zeroim echoes Genesis 1:29: the original Creator's diet before sin and empire. Daniel's refusal of the royal delicacies was not an ascetic whim; it was covenant loyalty to the Creator's design and Leviticus 11. Consecration at the table preceded revelation in the night.

H3068.derivation: From H1961 (hayah, “to be”): the self-Existent, Eternal One — Jehovah, the covenant Name. KJV prints LORD in small capitals; it is not a generic “god.”
H3068.gloss: the LORD — Israel’s covenant God (1890: the personal Name, not a title of Marduk).

danielHits.gloss: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet
I prayed unto the LORD my God — the Name in Daniel’s own confession
presenting my supplication before the LORD my God

otherKjv.gloss: I AM THAT I AM; this is my name for ever
the LORD names the end of Babylon’s seventy years
the LORD names Cyrus before the city falls

H3068.why: The covenant Name appears in Daniel only where Daniel himself speaks — chapter 9, the exile’s prayer. The empire chapters call Him the God of heaven; the prayer dares the Name that keeps covenant and mercy (9:4). The Lord of 1:2 is Adonai — the sovereign Master handing His own house to Babylon — and chapter 9 answers that hand-over with confession: the word of the LORD to Jeremiah, kept word for word.

H894.derivation: From H1101 balal, “to mix / confound” — the city of Genesis 11 remembered as confusion.
H894.gloss: Babylon / Babel (1890: the city and the kingdom, not a later church slogan).

danielHits.gloss: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon besieges Jerusalem
vessels carried to Shinar, to the house of his god

otherKjv.gloss: therefore is the name of it called Babel
Babylon hath been a golden cup in the LORD’s hand
Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, shall be as Sodom

H894.why: The gold head has a city with a genealogy: mixing and pride. Every later metal is measured from this fall. When chapter 5 drinks from the temple vessels, the Hebrew name of 1:1 has already told you whose house is being mocked.

H895.derivation: Aramaic twin of Hebrew H894. Same city, court language of chapters 2–7.
H895.gloss: Babylon (1890: the Aramaic spelling used when the king speaks).

danielHits.gloss: Is not this great Babylon that I have built
third ruler in the kingdom of Babylon

otherKjv.gloss: Cyrus king of Babylon — the name survives the transfer
thus shall Babylon sink

H895.why: The king names the city at the height of pride. Chapter 4’s boast and chapter 5’s feast use the same Aramaic word. The stump is left; the gold is not eternal.

H1351.derivation: Primitive root: to soil, desecrate, or pollute — the opposite of holy use.
H1351.gloss: to defile (1890: ceremonial and moral stain, not mere bad taste).

danielHits.gloss: Daniel would not defile himself with the king’s meat and wine

otherKjv.gloss: ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar
your hands are defiled with blood
her that is filthy and polluted

H1351.why: The first stand is at the table, before any dream is read. Leviticus 11 already sorted clean from unclean; the king’s portion had been poured to Marduk. Daniel can take a new name and a new language. He cannot take a polluted cup and still read sealed books.

H3117.derivation: From an unused root meaning to be hot; the daylight period, then a measured day.
H3117.gloss: day (1890: ordinary solar day; in appointed signs it can stand for a year).

danielHits.gloss: two thousand and three hundred days — then the sanctuary is cleansed
stand in thy lot at the end of the days

otherKjv.gloss: each day for a year shall ye bear your iniquities
I have appointed thee each day for a year
the evening and the morning were the first day

H3117.why: Numbers 14:34 and Ezekiel 4:6 do not invent a code; they show God already counting a day as a year when He appoints a sign. Daniel 9 then runs seventy weeks to a dated Messiah. That is why 8:14’s 2,300 days are not three years of Antiochus but a longer measured line.

H8141.derivation: From H8138, to fold / repeat — a year as a completed turn of seasons.
H8141.gloss: year (1890: a literal solar year, the other half of the year-day pair).

danielHits.gloss: third year of Jehoiakim
seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem

otherKjv.gloss: forty days become forty years
each day for a year
these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years

H8141.why: The year is the unit the day becomes. Jeremiah’s seventy years are ordinary years Daniel can count on a calendar. The seventy weeks of 9:24 use the appointed day-for-year scale so 490 days become 490 years. Two clocks, one God.

H7328.derivation: (Aramaic) a secret, a hidden matter — the word the court guilds admit they cannot reach (2:10-11).
H7328.gloss: secret (1890: a concealed matter Heaven must disclose).

danielHits.gloss: mercies concerning this secret; then the secret is revealed
God in heaven revealeth secrets
a revealer of secrets

otherKjv.gloss: no secret troubleth thee — the same word in the tree dream

H7328.why: Daniel 2:28 is a method statement. Magicians ask for the dream first because they cannot fetch a raz. Historicism starts here: the image is given, not guessed, and it runs from the prophet’s night to the latter days.

H1541.derivation: Corresponding to H1540 galah: to denude, disclose, make naked.
H1541.gloss: to reveal (1890: to uncover what was covered).

danielHits.gloss: the secret was revealed unto Daniel
there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets
a revealer of secrets

otherKjv.gloss: he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets
the secret things belong unto the LORD; the revealed things to us

H1541.why: The verb under “revealeth secrets” is the opposite of occult theft. Court science fails in 2:10–11. Prayer succeeds in 2:18–19. The sitting can name metals because Heaven uncovered them.

H6755.derivation: Corresponding to H6754: an image, idol, or representational form.
H6755.gloss: image / statue (1890: a figure that stands for something else).

danielHits.gloss: the great image of successive metals
the all-gold image on the plain of Dura

otherKjv.gloss: Hebrew tselem — man made in God’s image
the image of the beast that must be worshipped

H6755.why: Chapter 2’s tselem is history in metals — successive kingdoms, not concurrent local powers. Chapter 3’s tselem is a counter-creed: all gold, no silver. Revelation 13 later commands worship of another image. Dura is the rehearsal.

H1722.derivation: Corresponding to Hebrew H2091 zahab, gold. From a root of shimmering yellow; the metal of royalty and of the sanctuary.
H1722.gloss: gold (1890: the precious metal, then the first kingdom by Daniel’s own sentence).

danielHits.gloss: this image’s head was of fine gold
thou art this head of gold
an image of gold sixty by six cubits
golden vessels from Jerusalem used to praise gods of gold

otherKjv.gloss: silver and gold freely offered for the house of God in Jerusalem
the ark overlaid with pure gold — holy furniture, not a throne-boast
they shall bring gold and incense

H1722.why: Dehab can name a cup, a statue, or a kingdom. Daniel 2:38 is the only metal the prophet pins to a living man: thou art this head of gold. That sentence is what lets the sitting watch silver replace him. Ezra 7:15 then uses the same metal for the house of God — gold returned to worship — while Daniel 3 and 5 use it to defy the dream and to toast idols. The word does not mean “Babylon” by itself; 2:38 is the identification that makes the rest of the statue a timeline.

H3702.derivation: Corresponding to H3701: silver, money, the pale metal under gold.
H3702.gloss: silver (1890: the second metal; inferior in glory, legal in reach).

danielHits.gloss: breast and arms of silver
another kingdom inferior to thee
golden and silver vessels from the temple

otherKjv.gloss: the Medes, which shall not regard silver
given to the Medes and Persians
silver freely offered for the house of God

H3702.why: Silver is named before it arrives. 2:39 promises an inferior kingdom; 5:28 names the Medes and Persians on the plaster. The two arms of 2:32 match the bear raised on one side in 7:5 and the ram’s uneven horns in 8:3, 20.

H5174.derivation: Corresponding to H5154: copper / bronze — harder than gold, cheaper than silver.
H5174.gloss: brass / bronze (1890: the third metal; arms and culture that travel).

danielHits.gloss: belly and thighs of brass
a third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth

otherKjv.gloss: the rough goat is the king of Grecia
a leopard with four wings and four heads
mountains of brass — bronze as imperial hardness

H5174.why: Bronze is not named “Greece” in chapter 2. Chapter 8 supplies the name after the goat breaks the ram. The sitting reads backward: once 8:21 is on the table, the third metal has a people and a speed.

H6523.derivation: Corresponding to H1270 barzel, iron — the metal that breaks.
H6523.gloss: iron (1890: strength that bruises; the fourth kingdom).

danielHits.gloss: legs of iron; feet part of iron and clay
the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron
great iron teeth

otherKjv.gloss: a yoke of iron upon thy neck
thou shalt break them with a rod of iron
rule them with a rod of iron

H6523.why: Iron is the only metal that keeps going after the legs: it reappears in the feet mixed with clay, and in the fourth beast’s teeth. The fourth kingdom is one career — imperial, then divided — not a jump to a Seleucid footnote.

H2635.derivation: A clod or potsherd; baked clay, brittle beside iron.
H2635.gloss: clay (1890: potter’s ware; strength that cannot fuse).

danielHits.gloss: feet part of iron and part of clay
they shall mingle… but they shall not cleave

otherKjv.gloss: we are the clay, and thou our potter
as the clay is in the potter’s hand
ten kings out of the fourth kingdom

H2635.why: Clay is not a fifth world empire. It is the fracture inside the fourth. 2:43 is the physics: dynastic mingling and forced unions do not make one metal again. The stone strikes here, not in Babylon.

H69.derivation: Corresponding to H68: a stone, a built or cut piece of rock — not a mountain already standing.
H69.gloss: stone (1890: a cut stone; here, cut without hands).

danielHits.gloss: a stone cut out without hands smote the image
the God of heaven sets up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed

otherKjv.gloss: the stone which the builders refused
a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone
whosoever shall fall on that stone

H69.why: Daniel 2 uses eben, a stone that arrives, not tsur, a cliff already there. It does not reform the metals. It grinds them. 2:44 times it “in the days of these kings” — the divided feet — so the sitting will not place the kingdom in Constantine or in 539.

H6697.derivation: A cliff or sharp rock; God as the already-standing Rock.
H6697.gloss: rock / cliff (1890: a massif, not a cut building-stone).

danielHits.gloss: not the word Daniel 2 uses for the kingdom-stone

otherKjv.gloss: He is the Rock, his work is perfect
the LORD is my rock
in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength (tsur)

H6697.why: The contrast teaches method. If Daniel had wanted a mountain already on the map, Hebrew had tsur. He uses eben: something cut and thrown. The kingdom arrives; it is not a reform of Rome or a church already standing.

H4437.derivation: From H4430 melek, king — the realm and the reign, not only a crown.
H4437.gloss: kingdom (1890: dominion transferred from metal to metal, then taken by the stone).

danielHits.gloss: kingdom given, then inferior, then brass, then iron, then God’s
the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men
there was given him a kingdom

otherKjv.gloss: thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom
thy kingdom come
the kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord

H4437.why: Malku is the thing that moves. Gold does not fade into silver; the kingdom is given to another people (2:39; 5:28). The stone’s kingdom is not left to other people (2:44). That transfer-language is why the sitting reads successive empires, not overlapping local dynasties.

H1855.derivation: To crush to powder; corresponding to H1854 daqaq.
H1855.gloss: to break in pieces (1890: grind, not merely defeat).

danielHits.gloss: brake them to pieces; became like the chaff
it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms
the fourth beast brake in pieces

otherKjv.gloss: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small
on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder

H1855.why: Iron bruises; the stone grinds. Empires do not evolve into the mountain. They become chaff that the wind carries away. That verb keeps the Second Coming sudden and terminal.

H2423.derivation: From a root of life / living thing; here a predatory beast.
H2423.gloss: beast (1890: a living creature; in chapter 7, a kingdom as predator).

danielHits.gloss: four great beasts came up from the sea
these great beasts… are four kings
the fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom

otherKjv.gloss: let a beast’s heart be given unto him
a beast rise up out of the sea

H2423.why: Daniel 7 restages the metals as predators. 7:17 and 7:23 will not let you spiritualize them into moods: they are kings / a kingdom. Same four, new sermon — and a horn the metals did not yet show.

H744.derivation: Corresponding to H738: lion, the royal predator.
H744.gloss: lion (1890: Babylon again, now as a winged lion).

danielHits.gloss: the first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings

otherKjv.gloss: the lion is come up from his thicket — against Judah
Israel is a scattered sheep; the king of Assyria and Babylon as lions
the beast was like a leopard, feet as a bear, mouth as a lion

H744.why: Once 2:38 has named the head, the lion cannot be a different first kingdom. Wings plucked and a man’s heart are chapter 4 in beast-language: the gold king is humbled, then restored.

H1678.derivation: Corresponding to H1677: a bear, heavy and devouring.
H1678.gloss: bear (1890: Medo-Persia raised on one side).

danielHits.gloss: a bear… raised up itself on one side, three ribs in the mouth

otherKjv.gloss: I will stir up the Medes; they shall dash young men
a ram with two horns, one higher, the higher last
the ram’s horns are the kings of Media and Persia

H1678.why: Raised on one side is the later horn of the ram: Persia overtakes Media. The three ribs are the sitting’s historical match for Lydia, Babylon, and Egypt — the bear’s commanded meal, not a fourth metal.

H7162.derivation: Corresponding to H7161: a horn — strength, a king, or a power growing from a beast.
H7162.gloss: horn (1890: a king or kingdom growing out of a prior beast).

danielHits.gloss: ten horns; another little horn before whom three are plucked up
that horn made war with the saints and prevailed
ten kings; another shall subdue three and think to change times and laws

otherKjv.gloss: Hebrew qeren — the ram’s two horns named Media and Persia
ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns
the ten horns are ten kings

H7162.why: A horn is never a mood. 7:24 says the ten horns are ten kings, and another rises after them, diverse, and subdues three. That is a church-state power among the fragments of the fourth beast — after 476, not a Greek tyrant inside the leopard. The little horn of chapter 8 uses the Hebrew twin (H7161) on a sanctuary line; chapter 7’s Aramaic qeren is the political-religious career that wears out the saints and is judged when the court sits.

H2192.derivation: Corresponding to H2191: small in first appearance.
H2192.gloss: little / small (1890: diminutive at the start, not in reach).

danielHits.gloss: another little horn

otherKjv.gloss: a little horn which waxed exceeding great
though thou be little among the thousands of Judah

H2192.why: Little is the opening size, not the verdict. The same horn speaks great words, wears out saints, and lasts a measured time. Do not confuse first appearance with final scale.

H6268.derivation: From a root of advancing in age; the Ancient, the one already there.
H6268.gloss: Ancient (of days) (1890: the presiding Judge, not a later emperor).

danielHits.gloss: the Ancient of days did sit
one like the Son of man came to the Ancient of days
until the Ancient of days came

otherKjv.gloss: from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God
his head and his hairs were white like wool

H6268.why: The court sits in heaven before the stone strikes the earth. 7:9–10 is not the Second Coming scene of 2:34. Thrones are placed, books are opened, then the Son of man is brought near. Sequence is the sitting’s argument.

H1247.derivation: A son; paired with H606 enash, “man,” in 7:13.
H1247.gloss: son (1890: offspring; here the one like a son of man).

danielHits.gloss: one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven
the fourth man is like bar-Elahin — “a son of the gods” by the king’s polytheism, the Son of God by the fact

otherKjv.gloss: the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, coming in the clouds
ye shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven
one sat like unto the Son of man

H1247.why: Dominion is given, not seized (7:14). The clouds go to the Ancient of days first. That heavenly approach is why the sitting will not collapse 7:13 into only the last trumpet, and why 12:1 can still wait for Michael to stand.

H606.derivation: Corresponding to H582: a mortal, a human being.
H606.gloss: man / human (1890: frail humanity, contrasted with beasts).

danielHits.gloss: son of man — bar enash
let his heart be changed from man’s
eyes like the eyes of man

otherKjv.gloss: what is man, that thou art mindful of him
what is man… or the son of man

H606.why: The one like a son of man is human and more than a beast-king. The little horn also has eyes of a man — intelligence without the given kingdom of 7:14. Two uses of “man,” two destinies.

H1780.derivation: Judgment, a legal decision; corresponding to H1779.
H1780.gloss: judgment (1890: a court session with books, not a mood).

danielHits.gloss: the judgment was set, and the books were opened
judgment was given to the saints
the judgment shall sit, and they shall take away his dominion

otherKjv.gloss: God shall bring every work into judgment
the books were opened
he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world

H1780.why: 7:10 is a sitting court with opened books before 7:11 destroys the beast. That order is the sitting’s claim: Heaven reviews, then executes. Do not wait for the stone of chapter 2 to be the only judgment scene. The Ancient of days already convenes.

H5732.derivation: An appointed time; a set season, not a vague “era.”
H5732.gloss: time / appointed time (1890: a measured period).

danielHits.gloss: let seven times pass over him
a time and times and the dividing of time
lying counsels that must hold “till the time be changed” — a change Heaven alone can make

otherKjv.gloss: a time, times, and an half
a time, and times, and half a time
power… to continue forty and two months

H5732.why: One time, two times, and half a time is 3½ years of appointed days — 1,260 days. On the year-day scale already shown in Numbers 14 and Ezekiel 4, that is 1,260 years. The sitting places that span on the little horn’s career (538 to 1798), not on Antiochus’s three-year altar. Chapter 4’s seven times over one man stay ordinary years; chapter 7’s formula is the apocalyptic twin of 12:7 and Revelation 12–13. And 2:9 lets liars threaten only “till the time be changed” — the same word they cannot touch.

H1882.derivation: A royal edict or a religious law; what a king or God binds.
H1882.gloss: law / decree (1890: statute — civil or sacred).

danielHits.gloss: except we find it against him concerning the law of his God
the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not
think to change times and laws

otherKjv.gloss: the laws of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered
whosoever will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king
the decree went forth that the wise men should be slain

H1882.why: Chapter 6 collides two daths: the law of Daniel’s God and an unchangeable civil decree. Chapter 7:25 then says the horn thinks to change times and laws. Worship-law is the target, not a tax code. That is why Dura (commanded worship) and the den (banned prayer) belong on the same rail as 7:25.

H8133.derivation: To alter, change, or be different; corresponding to H8132.
H8133.gloss: to change (1890: to revise what was given).

danielHits.gloss: think to change times and laws
who… have changed the king’s word
he changeth the times and the seasons

otherKjv.gloss: that it be not changed
I am the LORD, I change not

H8133.why: 2:21 says God changes times and seasons. 7:25 says the horn thinks to. The verb is a usurpation of the prerogative already claimed for Heaven. Calendar and commandment are not small edits; they are the claim to sit in God’s seat.

H4483.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4487 manah: to count, appoint. The verb behind MENE — not the mina weight itself.
H4483.gloss: to number (1890: the audit is done — a counted sum, closed).

danielHits.gloss: God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it

otherKjv.gloss: teach us to number our days
he calleth them all by names… for that he is strong in power; not one faileth
he removeth kings, and setteth up kings

H4483.why: The gold kingdom is finished on a counted night. Numbering is not a threat; it is an audit already closed. Isaiah 45 has already named the man who opens the gates.

H8625.derivation: To weigh; a shekel as the standard weight.
H8625.gloss: to weigh (1890: to put in the balances).

danielHits.gloss: TEKEL; thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting

otherKjv.gloss: by him actions are weighed
let me be weighed in an even balance
a just weight and balance are the LORD’s

H8625.why: Weighed and found wanting is the sanctuary’s language, not a banker’s joke. Chapter 4 left a stump; chapter 5 finds no repentance in the grandson. The balances were already in the room.

H6537.derivation: To split, divide; also a play on Paras, Persia.
H6537.gloss: to divide (1890: to break in two and to name Persia).

danielHits.gloss: UPHARSIN — and they divide
PERES; thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians

otherKjv.gloss: another kingdom inferior to thee
to Cyrus… to open before him the two leaved gates

H6537.why: The word does double work: divide, and Persia. The sitting does not need a later historian to invent the transfer. The plaster already puns the conqueror’s name.

H5894.derivation: A watcher, a waking one; a heavenly sentinel.
H5894.gloss: watcher (1890: a holy sentinel from heaven, not a court magician).

danielHits.gloss: a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven
this matter is by the decree of the watchers
the king saw a watcher and an holy one

otherKjv.gloss: God in heaven revealeth secrets — same court, earlier night
bless the LORD, ye his angels, that excel in strength

H5894.why: Heaven, not court magic, sentences the gold king. The stump-and-band is a decree from above. Pride is diagnosed as beastliness by a watcher, not by a physician of Babylon.

H352.derivation: A ram; also a projecting pillar or a chief — strength that butts.
H352.gloss: ram (1890: the two-horned ram named in 8:20).

danielHits.gloss: a ram with two horns, one higher, the higher last
the ram… are the kings of Media and Persia

otherKjv.gloss: the bear raised on one side — same uneven pair
go up, O Elam; besiege, O Media
Cyrus king of Persia — the higher horn in history

H352.why: Chapter 8 does the sitting’s work for you: the ram is named. Two horns, one higher and later, is Persia overtaking Media. You do not need a later school to invent that identification.

H6842.derivation: A he-goat; from a root of leaping or departing.
H6842.gloss: he-goat (1890: the western goat named Grecia in 8:21).

danielHits.gloss: an he goat… touched not the ground; notable horn broken; four notable ones
the rough goat is the king of Grecia

otherKjv.gloss: leopard with four wings and four heads
a mighty king… his kingdom shall be broken toward the four winds

H6842.why: Named: Grecia. Touches not the ground: Alexander’s speed. The great horn breaks; four stand up. The little horn of 8:9 comes after that partition, so it cannot be the first Greek king, and it cannot stop at a three-year altar if 8:17 aims at the time of the end.

H7161.derivation: A horn; power, a king, or the horn of the altar.
H7161.gloss: horn (1890: the notable horn, then four, then the little horn of chapter 8).

danielHits.gloss: a notable horn between his eyes
the great horn was broken; four notable ones
a little horn which waxed exceeding great

otherKjv.gloss: Aramaic qeren — the little horn among the ten
he shall exalt the horn of his anointed
an horn of salvation

H7161.why: Chapter 8’s first horn is Alexander; the four are his successors; the little horn grows exceeding great toward the pleasant land and against the tamid. Scale (exceeding great) and horizon (time of the end) are why a tribute-paying Seleucid cannot exhaust the line. The Aramaic horn of chapter 7 is the western church-state career; this Hebrew horn tracks the same fourth-kingdom afterlife onto the sanctuary.

H8548.derivation: From an unused root meaning to stretch — continuance, indefinite extension; used only as an adjective: constant, regular, the continual.
H8548.gloss: continual / daily (1890: the standing ministry, not a one-off rite).

danielHits.gloss: the daily sacrifice was taken away; how long the vision concerning the daily
they shall take away the daily sacrifice
from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away

otherKjv.gloss: the continual burnt offering, morning and evening
two lambs day by day, for a continual burnt offering
he ever liveth to make intercession

H8548.why: Tamid is the standing work, not a three-year pause on an earthly altar in 167 B.C. The horn of chapter 8 magnifies itself to the prince of the host and casts down the place of his sanctuary. The sitting reads a counterfeit priesthood against Heaven’s continual ministry — a career that reaches the time of the end (8:17), not a Maccabean winter.

H6944.derivation: From H6942: apartness, holiness; the sanctuary or holy things.
H6944.gloss: holy / sanctuary (1890: what is set apart; in 8:14 the holy place put right).

danielHits.gloss: the sanctuary and the host trodden; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed
to anoint the most Holy
they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength

otherKjv.gloss: he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary
let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them
a minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle

H6944.why: The thing cleansed in 8:14 is qodesh. Leviticus 16 is the older grammar: the holy place is put right on the Day of Atonement. The sitting will not reduce that to Antiochus’s altar when 8:17 dates the vision to the time of the end and 9:24 still has a most Holy to anoint.

H6663.derivation: Primitive root: to be right in a moral or forensic sense; Niphal in 8:14, וְנִצְדַּק — “shall be put right.” Brown-Driver-Briggs: the holy place shall be put right, in a right condition; or be justified, its cause vindicated.
H6663.gloss: to justify / make right (1890: cleanse, clear, be just, justify — forensic, not a mop).

danielHits.gloss: then shall the sanctuary be cleansed (nitsdaq)
they that turn many to righteousness

otherKjv.gloss: the judges… shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked
shall my righteous servant justify many
how should man be just with God?

H6663.why: Nitsdaq is a court verb. Deuteronomy 25:1 uses the same root for a judge who justifies the righteous. Isaiah 53:11 uses it for the Servant who justifies many. Daniel 8:14 therefore does not mean “wash the stones in 164 B.C.” It means the holy place is vindicated — put back in the right, its cause cleared — after 2,300 appointed days. The sitting joins that verse to Leviticus 16’s Day of Atonement and to the opened books of 7:10. 457 + 2300 is arithmetic on a forensic word, not a slogan.

H2852.derivation: Primitive root: to cut off; figuratively to decree or determine. Hapax — this verb occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. BDB: divide, determine.
H2852.gloss: to cut off / determine (1890: KJV “determined”; the root is a cut, not a stretch).

danielHits.gloss: seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city

otherKjv.gloss: the only longer uncut line still on the table when Gabriel returns
none understood the 2,300 — chapter 9 is the explanation
understand the matter, and consider the vision — the vision just given

H2852.why: A hapax cannot hide. If seventy weeks are cut off, they are cut from a longer piece. The only longer piece Daniel has just been given is the 2,300 days (8:14, 26–27). Gabriel says “consider the vision” (9:23) while Daniel is still sick from that vision. That is why 457 B.C. (Ezra 7) starts both clocks, why A.D. 31 in the midst of the seventieth week seals the line, and why the remaining 1,810 years are not a second, disconnected puzzle.

H4899.derivation: From H4886 mashach, to smear / anoint — the anointed one.
H4899.gloss: Messiah / anointed (1890: the consecrated prince of 9:25-26).

danielHits.gloss: unto the Messiah the Prince
shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself

otherKjv.gloss: the rulers take counsel against the LORD, and against his anointed
the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings
we have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ

H4899.why: Cut off in the midst of the seventieth week. A.D. 31 is not a church tradition pasted on; it is the week’s midpoint once 457 + 483 lands on the baptism. That hit is what keeps the rest of the 2,300 honest.

H3772.derivation: To cut; used of cutting a covenant and of cutting off a life.
H3772.gloss: to cut off (1890: to kill, or to cut a covenant).

danielHits.gloss: shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself

otherKjv.gloss: he was cut off out of the land of the living
the LORD made (cut) a covenant with Abram
I will make a new covenant

H3772.why: Messiah is cut off, but not for himself. The cross, not a Roman prince, is the midst of the week (9:27). Futurism’s gap after week 69 has to ignore this cut and invent a later confirmer. The sitting will not.

H4317.derivation: Who is like God? From H4310 mi + H3588 ki + H410 El.

danielHits.gloss: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help
Michael your prince
at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince

otherKjv.gloss: Michael the archangel… disputed about the body of Moses
Michael and his angels fought against the dragon
as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come

H4317.why: The great prince who stands up. Intercession has a posture: a priest sits to minister and stands when the work is finished. 12:1 is that stand — then trouble, then names in a book, then dust that wakes. The sitting describes the scene; it does not need a later title for the court.

H5975.derivation: To stand, remain, or take a station; the opposite of sitting to serve.
H5975.gloss: to stand (1890: to arise to a finished office or a new act).

danielHits.gloss: Michael shall stand up
there shall stand up yet three kings… a mighty king shall stand up
he shall also stand up against the Prince of princes

otherKjv.gloss: every priest standeth daily… but this man, after he had offered one sacrifice, sat down
the Son of man standing on the right hand of God
then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment

H5975.why: A priest sits to minister and stands when the work is finished. Michael stands up. The sitting reads 12:1 as the end of that heavenly work, then the trouble, then the waking — not as a military footnote in Persia.

H6869.derivation: Tightness, distress; a strait that closes in.
H6869.gloss: trouble / distress (1890: a time of straitness, not ordinary war).

danielHits.gloss: a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation

otherKjv.gloss: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it
then shall be great tribulation, such as was not
a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress

H6869.why: The trouble comes after Michael stands, not before. Sequence again: finished advocacy, then the strait, then deliverance for those written in the book. The sitting will not relocate 12:1 into 605 or 167.

H6083.derivation: Dust, dry earth; the stuff of Genesis 2:7 and of graves.
H6083.gloss: dust (1890: the soil the dead sleep in).

danielHits.gloss: them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake

otherKjv.gloss: dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return
thy dead men shall live… awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust
though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God

H6083.why: The dead sleep in the dust. The hope is bodily rising, not a chart and not a disembodied slogan. 12:2 is the book’s last doctrine: two awakenings, two destinies.

H6974.derivation: To awake from sleep; used of the dead in 12:2.
H6974.gloss: to awake (1890: to rise from sleep — here, from death).

danielHits.gloss: many… shall awake, some to everlasting life, some to shame

otherKjv.gloss: awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust
all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth
the dead in Christ shall rise first

H6974.why: Daniel 12:2 is resurrection, not metaphor. The sitting ends on bodies, not on a party name. That is why Michael’s stand is not the last word — the lot of 12:13 is.

H1486.derivation: A pebble used for lots; then the allotted portion itself.
H1486.gloss: lot / allotted portion (1890: the share assigned, not chance).

danielHits.gloss: thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days

otherKjv.gloss: Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh
the LORD is the portion of mine inheritance… the lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places
the inheritance of the saints in light

H1486.why: Daniel’s last word is rest, then stand in thy lot. The sealed book does not end in fear. It ends in an assigned place at the end of the days — the same days 8:14 and 12:13 have been counting.

H2377.derivation: From H2372: a sight, a revelation, a prophetic vision.
H2377.gloss: vision (1890: a disclosed sight, not a private mood).

danielHits.gloss: Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams
at the time of the end shall be the vision
shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days

otherKjv.gloss: the vision is yet for an appointed time… though it tarry, wait for it
where there is no vision, the people perish
consider the vision

H2377.why: The vision is for the time of the end (8:17, 19) and for many days (8:26). That pair rules out a fulfillment that dies in 164 B.C. Gabriel’s “consider the vision” in 9:23 ties the seventy weeks to this same chazon.

H8269.derivation: A head person, captain, or prince — civil or heavenly.
H8269.gloss: prince (1890: a ruler; in chapter 10, also a heavenly counterpart).

danielHits.gloss: the prince of the host
the Prince of princes
the prince of the kingdom of Persia
Michael your prince

otherKjv.gloss: the Prince of Peace
captain of the host of the LORD
Messiah the Prince

H8269.why: Prince of Persia, prince of Grecia, Michael your prince. Behind the metals is a war of princes. The sitting will not read chapter 11 as only newspapers. The same word binds 8:11, 9:25, and 12:1 into one office argued against a counterfeit.

H136.derivation: Emphatic form of H113 adon (master, lord): my Lord — used as a proper name of God only.
H136.gloss: the Lord / Lord (1890: the sovereign Master; KJV prints Lord for Adonai, LORD for H3068 YHWH).

danielHits.gloss: the Lord gave Jehoiakim into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand
I set my face unto the Lord God

otherKjv.gloss: O Lord, send by the hand of him whom thou wilt send
O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name
The LORD God is my strength

H136.why: Daniel 1:2 will not let Babylon write the first sentence: the Lord (Adonai) gave. The Master hands His own house over — this is ownership, not defeat. Chapter 9 then opens with the same word: Daniel sets his face unto the Lord God. Master in chapter 1, confessor in chapter 9 — the sitting learns who really signs the transfer papers.

H430.derivation: Plural of H433 elowahh: God — the Creator’s ordinary name, used even of false gods by context.
H430.gloss: God (1890: the same word names the house of God and the house of “his god” in one verse).

danielHits.gloss: the vessels of the house of God carried to the house of his god

otherKjv.gloss: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth
God standeth in the congregation of the mighty

H430.why: One word for two houses in 1:2: the vessels move from the house of Elohim to the house of his elohim. Moses’ word never flatters an idol; context convicts it. The theft is house-to-house — and 2:37 answers it: the God of heaven gave Nebuchadnezzar the kingdom. Chapter 9:4 then kneels before the LORD my God — the same Elohim, personally held.

H3063.derivation: From H3034 yadah, to praise: “praised” — Leah’s word at his birth.
H3063.gloss: Judah (1890: the praised tribe; the tribe of the coming Lion).

danielHits.gloss: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jehoiakim king of Judah

otherKjv.gloss: she called his name Judah: Now will I praise
Judah is a lion’s whelp… the sceptre shall not depart
the Lion of the tribe of Juda

H3063.why: The first verse names the conquered nation — the tribe of praise, the tribe of the sceptre, the tribe of the Lion. Babylon’s war is against that line. The book’s own beasts (7:4-6) are the counter-claimants, and the sitting keeps Genesis 49:10 on the table: the sceptre does not depart; it is handed about by permission until the Son of man receives it (7:13-14).

H3389.derivation: A dual form: “double peace” — from the Salem of Genesis 14 and shalom.
H3389.gloss: Jerusalem (1890: the city of peace, besieged in the book’s first verse).

danielHits.gloss: Nebuchadnezzar comes against Jerusalem and besieges it

otherKjv.gloss: Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem
when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it

H3389.why: The city of peace opens the book under siege. Daniel 6:10 will show an old man praying toward this Jerusalem with open windows, and 9:2 reading her seventy years. The sitting keeps the city in view because 9:25-26 dates her rebuilding and her destruction — peace is a promise under discipline, not a slogan.

H5019.derivation: Of Babylonian origin — the name invokes Nebo, the god of writing and borders: “Nebo, protect the boundary.”
H5019.gloss: Nebuchadnezzar (1890: the conqueror whose name borrows a god’s protection).

danielHits.gloss: king of Babylon, sweeps down on Jerusalem

otherKjv.gloss: Jehoiakim became his servant three years
Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant

H5019.why: His name is a prayer to Nebo — protect my border. God lets the border-crosser cross, then teaches him borders of a different kind: seven times with a beast’s heart, until his eyes lift to heaven (4:34). The sitting watches the name fail while the God it ignored still rules the boundary it promised to keep.

H8152.derivation: Of foreign origin; the plain where Babel was built — the land remembered from Genesis 11.
H8152.gloss: Shinar (1890: the Genesis-11 address of Babylon; the sitting’s wayback sign).

danielHits.gloss: the vessels are carried into the land of Shinar

otherKjv.gloss: the beginning of his kingdom was Babel… in the land of Shinar
they found a plain in the land of Shinar
to build it an house in the land of Shinar

H8152.why: Daniel could say “Babylon”; he says “Shinar” — the zip code of Babel’s tower, where mankind first mixed religion and empire into one building. Zechariah later sees wickedness carried back there in a house built for it. The vessels of chapter 5 are drunk from in Shinar’s temple; the sitting reads chapter 1 as a relocation to the oldest crime scene.

H3478.derivation: From H8280 sarah, to strive with God: “God strives” / “prevails with God” — Jacob’s new name.
H3478.gloss: Israel (1890: the covenant name of the people and of the prince who intercedes).

danielHits.gloss: certain of the children of Israel carried to the court
confessing my sin, and the sin of my people Israel

otherKjv.gloss: Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel

H3478.why: The name means the wrestling is real and God prevails. Exile children carry it into Babylon’s academy (1:3); chapter 9 makes it a confession (9:20); 12:1 promises “thy people… every one found written in the book.” The sitting will not spiritualize the name away: Israel’s story, exile and all, is the spine the metals hang on.

H2233.derivation: From H2232 zara', to sow: seed — posterity as sown grain.
H2233.gloss: seed (1890: royal seed here; promise-seed everywhere).

danielHits.gloss: of the king’s seed, and of the princes

otherKjv.gloss: it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel
in thy seed shall all the nations be blessed

H2233.why: Babylon collects the king’s seed — and cannot see it is collecting the promise-seed’s carriers. Genesis 3:15 and 22:18 put everything on a Seed. Exile, furnace, den, and court cannot uproot it; 9:26 will cut off the Messiah as if the Seed failed — and 7:13-14 shows the Seed enthroned.

H5631.derivation: From an unused root meaning to be castrated; a eunuch — court official or chamberlain.
H5631.gloss: eunuch / officer (1890: Ashpenaz, master of the eunuchs — the official over the body of the court).

danielHits.gloss: the master of his eunuchs is ordered to bring the youth

otherKjv.gloss: Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh
the eunuchs that stood about him

H5631.why: The eunuch’s office is custody of persons. Ashpenaz owns names, diets, and futures — and Daniel’s kindness wins him (1:9). The sitting notes the chain of custody: kings command through officers, but God holds the officer’s fear (1:9-10) and the boy’s conscience (1:8).

H3778.derivation: Of foreign origin: a Chaldean — Abraham’s own district (Ur of the Chaldees), later the learned caste of Babylon.
H3778.gloss: Chaldean (1890: both a people and the court guild of astrologer-scholars).

danielHits.gloss: the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans
the Chaldeans summoned with the magicians

otherKjv.gloss: Haran died… in Ur of the Chaldees
I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation

H3778.why: The tongue Daniel must learn belongs to a guild that failed at 2:10-11. Habakkuk calls the nation “bitter and hasty” (Hab 1:6); Daniel outstudies it (1:20) without owning its spirits. The sitting uses the word twice: a bloodline from Abraham’s homeland, and a science-school that cannot read the dream.

H4093.derivation: From H3045 yada', to know: knowledge, science — knowing as a possession.
H4093.gloss: knowledge / science (1890: court-learning; Daniel receives it from God, not from the guild).

danielHits.gloss: cunning in knowledge, and understanding science
God gave them knowledge and skill

otherKjv.gloss: Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people

H4093.why: Outside Daniel, madda’ occurs only in Solomon’s prayer for a knowing heart (2 Chron 1:10-12). Here it is God-given twice: the curriculum (1:4) and the gift (1:17). The sitting separates the school from the Spirit — Daniel aces the science and keeps the Source.

H2451.derivation: From H2449 chakam, to be wise: wisdom — skill applied, not theory owned.
H2451.gloss: wisdom (1890: the craftsman’s word — Bezaleel had it; Daniel has it; so does the serpent in Eden).

danielHits.gloss: skilful in all wisdom
ten times better in all matters of wisdom and understanding

otherKjv.gloss: I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom
Wisdom is the principal thing

H2451.why: The word that built the tabernacle now outbuilds Babylon (1:20: ten times better). Wisdom is direction-neutral — it is skill with hands or with words. The sitting asks whose purposes it serves: God filled Bezaleel for a sanctuary and Daniel for a courtroom; Babylon seeks it for prognostication and gets silence (2:10-11).

H1847.derivation: From H3045 yada', to know: knowledge.
H1847.gloss: knowledge (1890: knowing as discernment; the famine-word of Hosea 4:6).

danielHits.gloss: cunning in knowledge
knowledge shall be increased

otherKjv.gloss: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge

H1847.why: The book opens with court-knowledge captured (1:4) and closes with knowledge increasing worldwide (12:4). Hosea warned that destruction runs on a knowledge-famine; Amos ran the opposite famine of hearing (8:12); Daniel 12 dates the thaw. The sitting reads the “increase of knowledge” as the sealed book opening — travel and printing included, prophecy understood first.

H7919.derivation: A primitive root: to be circumspect and hence intelligent — to prosper by prudent dealing.
H7919.gloss: skill / understand / prosper (1890: the maskil’s verb — insight that acts).

danielHits.gloss: God gave them knowledge and skill
they that be wise shall shine

otherKjv.gloss: my servant shall deal prudently (yaskil)
he that gathereth in summer is a wise son

H7919.why: Skill (1:17) and the shining wise (12:3) are the same root. Isaiah pinned it on the Servant who deals prudently and on the many He justifies. The sitting ties the pair: Daniel’s cohort learns to prosper under pagan kings; the end-time wise turn many to righteousness and inherit the shine.

H5612.derivation: From H5608 caphar, to count or rehearse: a writing — scroll, book, register.
H5612.gloss: book / learning (1890: KJV renders it “learning” in 1:4 and “books” in 9:2 — both are writings).

danielHits.gloss: teach them the learning of the Chaldeans
I understood by books the number of the years
seal the book, even to the time of the end

otherKjv.gloss: the vision of all is become to you as… a book that is sealed
a book written within and on the backside, sealed

H5612.why: A word with two jobs: Babylon’s literature Daniel masters, and Heaven’s register Daniel obeys. By 12:4 the writing is sealed until the time of the end, and the same era answers with running to and fro and increasing knowledge. The sitting holds the two uses together — God out-writes Babylon and seals the difference.

H6598.derivation: Of Persian origin: a choice portion of food — the king’s ration.
H6598.gloss: portion / meat (1890: a Persian loan-word for the royal delicacies; appears only in Daniel 1 and 11:26).

danielHits.gloss: a daily portion of the king’s meat
that he might not defile himself with the portion

H6598.why: The ration is diplomacy: eat the king’s food, live the king’s life, owe the king your body. Daniel declines the portion and keeps the conscience (1:8) — and gains the table anyway (1:15-16). The sitting reads the menu as allegiance: one meal at a time, the exile chooses whose covenant he eats under.

H3196.derivation: From an unused root meaning to effervesce: wine.
H3196.gloss: wine (1890: the drink of kings and of cornered prophets).

danielHits.gloss: and of the wine which he drank
he would not defile himself with the wine

otherKjv.gloss: Wine is a mocker
wine that maketh glad the heart of man
he drank of the wine, and was drunken

H3196.why: The king’s wine offers friendship on his terms. Daniel drinks water with his pulse and outshines the table (1:15). The sitting keeps Proverbs 20:1 next to the choice: the mocker stays in Babylon’s cup; the court of chapter 7 runs on no one’s intoxication but Heaven’s schedule.

H5254.derivation: A primitive root: to test, prove, assay — to put to the proof for verification.
H5254.gloss: prove / test (1890: Daniel proposes the ten-day assay).

danielHits.gloss: Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days

otherKjv.gloss: God did tempt (prove) Abraham
to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart
prove me now herewith

H5254.why: The verb God uses on Abraham Daniel borrows on himself — ten days, watch the results. Testing is how Scripture verifies faith, not how it plays games. The sitting notes who requests the test: the testee volunteers, and the tester (God) grades in public (1:15).

H1095.derivation: Of Babylonian origin: “Bel, protect the king” — the new name given to Daniel.
H1095.gloss: Belteshazzar (1890: Daniel’s court name; the record keeps calling him Daniel anyway).

danielHits.gloss: unto Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar
the king answers and says to Belteshazzar — and the prophet still speaks as himself
named according to the name of my god

otherKjv.gloss: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth

H1095.why: Babylon renames people to re-own them. The god in the name is Bel — the same god Isaiah already sentenced to bow. Daniel never objects to the label and never adopts its loyalty: the court hears Belteshazzar; the book keeps saying Daniel, God-is-my-judge. Identity sits deeper than vocabulary.

H2608.derivation: From H2603 chanan (to favor) + H3050 Yah: “Yah has been gracious.”

danielHits.gloss: to Hananiah, Shadrach

otherKjv.gloss: Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, of Gibeon
Hananiah… a faithful man, and feared God above many

H2608.why: Yah has been gracious — written into a boy shipped to Babylon. Jeremiah’s Hananiah wore the same name while prophesying lies; grace is in the Giver, not the syllables. The sitting keeps the God-names (Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael) audible under the court names: the furnace will answer for them.

H7714.derivation: Of Babylonian origin: “command of Aku” — Aku the moon-god.
H7714.gloss: Shadrach (1890: the moon-god’s command wearing a servant of Yah).

danielHits.gloss: he gave to Hananiah the name Shadrach

H7714.why: A moon-god’s order replaces “Yah has been gracious” — that is the renaming’s theology in one swap. The furnace scene then shows whose word actually governs fire (3:27). The sitting lets the court keep its names while the record keeps its God.

H4332.derivation: From H4310 miy (who), H834 asher (what), and H410 El: “who is what God is?”
H4332.gloss: Mishael (1890: the God-name behind Meshach — an identity question aimed at every idol).

danielHits.gloss: to Mishael, Meshach

otherKjv.gloss: Mishael and Elzaphan… sons of Uzziel

H4332.why: The name is a question: who is like God? — unanswerable by Babylon’s inventory. The court answers with Meshach (H4335), a name of Aku; the furnace answers with the fourth man (3:25). The sitting hears Mishael’s question all the way to Michael — who is like God? (10:13, 21; 12:1).

H4335.derivation: Of Babylonian origin: probably “who is like Aku?” — the moon-god parodied as the answer to Mishael’s question.

danielHits.gloss: to Mishael, Meshach

H4335.why: Babylon rewrites the question “who is like God?” into “who is like Aku?” — a parody, not an answer. The book lets the parody stand in the roster and lets the fire field the real question. The sitting watches parody meet the fourth man and lose.

H5838.derivation: From H5826 azar (to help) + H3050 Yah: “Yah has helped.”

danielHits.gloss: and to Azariah, Abed-nego

otherKjv.gloss: Azariah… king of Judah
My help cometh from the LORD

H5838.why: Yah has helped — named over a boy the empire is buying. The furnace becomes the proof of the name: no helper but Yah enters fire, and one walks in it unharmed (3:25). The sitting keeps the Hebrew meaning audible under Abed-nego’s syllables.

H5664.derivation: From H5650 ebed (servant) + Nego (Nebo): “servant of Nebo.”
H5664.gloss: Abed-nego (1890: the court name — a servant-title under the writing-god).

danielHits.gloss: to Azariah, Abed-nego

otherKjv.gloss: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth

H5664.why: Servant of Nebo — the empire’s ideal résumé. The record answers with a greater service: the same three who will not serve the image (3:18) are served by Heaven’s angel (3:28). The sitting tracks “serve” through the chapter like a litmus strip.

H2748.derivation: Of Egyptian origin: a horoscopist — the priest-scholar of court divination (Joseph met the breed in Egypt).
H2748.gloss: magician (1890: the engraver of omens; the guild that fails in Daniel 2).

danielHits.gloss: the king found them ten times better than all the magicians
the king commands the magicians to be called

otherKjv.gloss: Pharaoh… called for all the magicians of Egypt
the wise men and the sorcerers of Egypt

H2748.why: Egypt’s court-magicians reappear in Babylon with the same job description and the same ceiling: they can repeat tricks, not reveal secrets (2:10-11). Daniel outstudies them tenfold (1:20) and never joins their craft. The sitting uses chartom as the standing emblem of court-science without revelation.

H826.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to ashshaph: astrologer — the guild-word in 2:10; 4:6; 5:7, 11, 15 (1:20 and 2:2 use the plural form H825).
H826.gloss: astrologer (1890: the conjurer caste; appears in Daniel 1–5 and nowhere else in the Bible).

danielHits.gloss: the king commands the astrologers to be brought before the tree-dream
the astrologers called again on the wall-night — and cannot read
the queen remembers Daniel, whom the astrologers could not match

H826.why: A Daniel-only word for a Daniel-only rival: the star-whisperers. The book stages their failure repeatedly (2:10-11; 4:6-7; 5:8-9) while Heaven discloses freely. The sitting reads the guild as the standing picture of divination without covenant.

H2472.derivation: From H2492 chalam, to be healthy or dream: a dream.
H2472.gloss: dream (1890: God’s oldest night-channel — Abimelech, Jacob, Joseph, Solomon).

danielHits.gloss: Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams
Nebuchadnezzar dreams dreams

otherKjv.gloss: God came to Abimelech in a dream by night
your old men shall dream dreams
Joseph dreamed a dream

H2472.why: Chapter 1 ends with the gift certified (1:17); chapter 2 opens with the exam (2:1). Dreams are God’s mail, not the guild’s property — which is why the court can neither recall nor read this one. The sitting pairs the certificate with the crisis the way Scripture pairs gifting and assignment.

H3566.derivation: Of foreign origin (Persian): Cyrus — “sun/throne,” the Persian monarch named by Isaiah before his birth.
H3566.gloss: Cyrus (1890: the king who ends the exile Daniel outlived).

danielHits.gloss: Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus

otherKjv.gloss: that saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd
Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus
Cyrus king of Persia made a proclamation

H3566.why: Daniel’s ministry runs to Cyrus (1:21) — the one stop-clock in the book’s first chapter. Isaiah had named this man two centuries early as the shepherd who releases the exiles. The sitting lets 1:21 foreshadow chapter 9: Daniel counts years because God sets years, and the countdown’s landing is a decree, not luck.

H3820.derivation: From an unused root meaning to be enclosed: the heart — the enclosed control-room of will and conscience.
H3820.gloss: heart (1890: purposed — the decision-factory, not the sentiment).

danielHits.gloss: Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself

otherKjv.gloss: the meditation of my heart
the LORD looketh on the heart

H3820.why: Before any dream, any promotion, any furnace — a decision in an enclosed room. The lebab purposes once and the body follows for seventy years. The sitting marks the word because every later victory in the book is downstream of this private vote.

H2376.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2377 chazon: a sight, a vision.
H2376.gloss: vision (1890: the night-vision that hands Daniel the king’s secret).

danielHits.gloss: then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision

H2376.why: Daniel receives the dream in a vision of his own — the king got the problem asleep, the prophet got the answer awake. The Aramaic twin of chazon (H2377) keeps one vocabulary for both languages: sight is disclosed, never deduced.

H7093.derivation: From H7092 qatsats (to cut off): an end — a terminus, the far edge of a set period.
H7093.gloss: end (1890: in “the time of the end” — a dated horizon, not a mood).

danielHits.gloss: at the time of the end shall be the vision
at the time of the end the king of the south pushes at him
seal the book, even to the time of the end
stand in thy lot at the end of the days

otherKjv.gloss: the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak

H7093.why: Qets is a cut-off point. Habakkuk 2:3 is the control text: the vision tarries to an appointed end and then speaks — it does not die in antiquity. The sitting uses 8:17 and 12:4 the same way: the prophecy is dated to the end’s neighborhood, and 12:13 lets the old prophet himself stand there.

H6153.derivation: From arab, to grow dark: evening — the day’s hinge.
H6153.gloss: evening (1890: half of the sanctuary’s counting unit; KJV renders the 2,300 as “days”).

danielHits.gloss: two thousand and three hundred days — the Hebrew counts evenings and mornings; KJV renders the unit “days”
about the time of the evening oblation

otherKjv.gloss: the evening and the morning were the first day

H6153.why: Genesis 1:5 sets the pairing: evening plus morning is one day. The 2,300 are counted in those sanctuary units — the KJV’s “days” translates a clock made of hinges. The sitting points at 9:21: the evening lamb-hour still beats in exile; 8:14 counts in its rhythm.

H1242.derivation: From baqar, to break forth: morning — dawn as breaking-out.
H1242.gloss: morning (1890: the other hinge of the 2,300; joy comes in it — Psalm 30:5).

danielHits.gloss: two thousand and three hundred evening-morning units; KJV renders “days”

otherKjv.gloss: the evening and the morning were the first day
joy cometh in the morning

H1242.why: The word is breaking-forth — dawn as deliverance. In 8:14 it completes the day-unit of the longest prophecy, and its partner joy-cometh-in-the-morning suits a verse that ends the book’s longest night. The sitting counts with the sanctuary, not with the KJV’s smoothing.

H6588.derivation: From pasha, to rebel or transgress: a breach of relationship — revolt, not an accident.
H6588.gloss: transgression (1890: rebellion with a face; the thing the 490 must finish).

danielHits.gloss: the transgression of desolation
to finish the transgression

otherKjv.gloss: he was wounded for our transgressions
pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression

H6588.why: Pesha’ is revolt — sin as insurrection. The little horn’s transgression desolates (8:13); the seventy weeks are cut to finish transgression (9:24) — and Isaiah says the wounded Servant carried it. The sitting joins 8:14 and 9:24 through this word: both verdicts aim at the rebellion, and the cross stands inside the arithmetic.

H8074.derivation: A primitive root: to stun or devastate — to grow numb, to be appalled; hence desolate.
H8074.gloss: desolate / make desolate (1890: the covenant-curse word — what the abomination does).

danielHits.gloss: the transgression of desolation
he shall make it desolate
the abomination that maketh desolate
the abomination that maketh desolate set up

otherKjv.gloss: I will bring your sanctuaries unto desolation

H8074.why: Leviticus 26 wrote the threat into the covenant: unfaithfulness brings sanctuaries to shamem. Daniel 8-12 tracks the clause being executed — and 8:14 answers it with nitsdaq, the sanctuary put right. The sitting reads abomination/desolation as covenant lawsuit language, not architecture talk.

H6635.derivation: From tsaba', to mass or go forth: a host — army, service, the ordered array of heaven.
H6635.gloss: host (1890: the armies of heaven and their Prince).

danielHits.gloss: he magnified himself even to the prince of the host
the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot

otherKjv.gloss: as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come
all the host of heaven standing by him

H6635.why: The war behind the wars: a host with a Prince. The little horn’s crime is personal — magnified against the commander, then trampling His service and army. The sitting lets tsaba’ frame chapters 8 and 10-12 as one theater: heaven’s order contested on earth.

H4720.derivation: From H6942 qadash (to set apart): a set-apart place — sanctuary.
H4720.gloss: sanctuary (1890: the targeted holy place in ch. 8, 9, and 11).

danielHits.gloss: the place of his sanctuary was cast down
cause thy face to shine upon thy sanctuary that is desolate
they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength

otherKjv.gloss: let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them

H4720.why: Exodus 25:8 built the sanctuary so God could dwell with people; Daniel tracks the powers that trespass it. Chapter 8’s horn casts it down; chapter 9 dates its verdicts; chapter 11 pollutes it. The sitting will not let “sanctuary” drift into metaphor: it is the address of atonement, the very thing 8:14 says gets put right.

H2380.derivation: Feminine of H2374 (from chazah, to see): a sight — something conspicuous.

danielHits.gloss: a notable horn between his eyes

H2380.why: Notable means you cannot miss it: the great horn is fame at full speed. The sitting contrasts scale and start — the goat’s first horn announces itself; the little horn of 8:9 begins small and grows exceeding great. Visibility is not verdict; timing and conduct are.

H6643.derivation: From tsabah, to desire: beauty, glory — the gazelle’s grace, the land’s delight.
H6643.gloss: pleasant / glorious (1890: “the pleasant land” — Jerusalem’s country named by its beauty).

danielHits.gloss: the little horn waxes great toward the pleasant land
he stands in the glorious land
he plants the tents of his palace… in the glorious holy mountain

otherKjv.gloss: the branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious

H6643.why: The land is named by its comeliness — the country of the Branch. The little horn’s face is set toward that beauty, and chapter 11 tracks the trespass to the glorious mountain itself. The sitting keeps the geography honest: this war aims at the same city chapter 1 besieged.

H7962.derivation: From shalah, to be tranquil: ease, security — quietness that can be a weapon.
H7962.gloss: peace / ease (1890: “by peace shall he destroy many”).

danielHits.gloss: by peace shall he destroy many

otherKjv.gloss: Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces
when they shall say, Peace and safety

H7962.why: Shalvah is not always shalom: false ease disarms before it destroys. Daniel 8:25 names the horn’s method — policy and flattery, prosperity as a siege-engine. The sitting contrasts it with 8:14’s true peace: a sanctuary put right is the only shalvah that survives the audit.

H7665.derivation: A primitive root: to burst, break in pieces — collapse from within or by blow.
H7665.gloss: broken (1890: the horn “shall be broken without hand”).

danielHits.gloss: he shall be broken without hand
the arms of a flood… shall be broken

H7665.why: Broken without hand — the same without-hand family as 2:34’s stone. The sitting pairs them: the stone cut without hands breaks the image; the horn that stood against the Prince of princes is broken without one. Sovereignty always ends the argument unassisted.

H6918.derivation: From H6942 qadash: set apart — holy, apartness applied.
H6918.gloss: holy one / saint (1890: “one saint… another saint” in 8:13 — heaven’s interpreters).

danielHits.gloss: one saint speaking, and another saint asking the question

otherKjv.gloss: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts
be holy; for I am holy

H6918.why: The Hebrew sibling of Aramaic qaddiysh (H6922): the word for heaven’s holy ones and for God’s own character. In 8:13 the saints conduct the interview that gets the 2,300 answered. The sitting hears the question as liturgy — heaven asks how long, heaven answers by calendar.

H7620.derivation: Passive participle of H7650 shaba' (to seven oneself, swear): a “sevening” — a week of days or years.
H7620.gloss: week (1890: seventy sevens — the unit itself carries seven; the year-day scale makes them sevens of years).

danielHits.gloss: seventy weeks are determined
unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks
after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off
in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice to cease

otherKjv.gloss: fulfil her week — Jacob’s week of days

H7620.why: Jacob served a week of days for Rachel; Daniel’s weeks are sevens of years on the year-day scale. The word itself is sworn — sevened. The sitting watches the seventieth week split at the cross: Messiah confirms (H1396) and is cut off mid-week, and the remaining part runs on the same clock, not a gap.

H1285.derivation: From barah, to cut: a covenant — a cut-and-bound compact (hence H3772 karath, to cut a covenant).
H1285.gloss: covenant (1890: the covenant kept in heaven, claimed in exile, attacked by the horn).

danielHits.gloss: keeping the covenant and mercy
the prince of the covenant
indignation against the holy covenant

otherKjv.gloss: the LORD made a covenant with Abram
the blood of the covenant
I will put my law in their inward parts

H1285.why: Daniel prays the covenant from a foreign county (9:4) — keeping is God’s verb first. Chapter 11 shows a dynasty set against the holy covenant, and 9:27 gives Messiah the confirming week. The sitting binds 9:24-27 to 11:28-32: one covenant, defended from heaven, assaulted on earth.

H2617.derivation: From chasad, to be kind: covenant-loyalty — lovingkindness that keeps terms.
H2617.gloss: mercy / lovingkindness (1890: the loyalty-word God binds to His covenant).

danielHits.gloss: keeping the covenant and mercy

otherKjv.gloss: shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments
the mercy of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him

H2617.why: 9:4 quotes Exodus 20:6 almost clause for clause — Daniel prays in covenant vocabulary on purpose. Chesed is loyalty with staying power; the exile leans on it while counting seventy years. The sitting notes the quotation: Daniel does not invent comfort; he cites the terms.

H8104.derivation: A primitive root: to hedge about, guard, keep — as a watchman or shepherd.
H8104.gloss: keep (1890: God keeps covenant; saints keep commandments — one word, two directions).

danielHits.gloss: keeping the covenant… to them that keep his commandments

otherKjv.gloss: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee
he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep

H8104.why: Double keeping in one verse: the God who keeps terms, the people who keep them back. Psalm 121 says His keeping never sleeps; Daniel 9 says His keeping was the exile’s only ground. The sitting reads 9:4 as the posture for the whole book — kept, therefore obedient even in Babylon.

H4687.derivation: From H6680 tsavah, to command: a commandment.
H4687.gloss: commandment (1890: the terms of the covenant being kept in 9:4).

danielHits.gloss: to them that keep his commandments

otherKjv.gloss: them that keep my commandments
the commandments… to fear the LORD

H4687.why: The commandments in 9:4 are the ones Exodus 20 tied to mercy — Daniel prays the Sinai sentence back to God. The sitting lets the word anchor Daniel’s obedience (1:8, 6:10) to the same law the little horn intends to change (7:25).

H3414.derivation: From H7311 rum (to raise) and H3050 Yah: “Yah will raise” — Jeremiah’s name is a promise.
H3414.gloss: Jeremiah (1890: the prophet whose seventy years Daniel is reading).

danielHits.gloss: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, concerning the seventy years

otherKjv.gloss: to whom the word of the LORD came in the days of Josiah

H3414.why: Daniel reads a living letter whose author’s name says Yah will raise. The seventy years he counts are Jeremiah’s own words (Jer 25:11-12) — Scripture read with a calendar in hand. The sitting marks the name because chapter 9 is what Bible study looks like when prophecy is trusted.

H5030.derivation: From naba, to prophesy (to bubble up, pour forth): a spokesman — one through whom God pours words.
H5030.gloss: prophet / prophecy (1890: the mouth God borrows).

danielHits.gloss: whereof the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet
to seal up the vision and prophecy

otherKjv.gloss: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren

H5030.why: Two uses bracket chapter 9: Jeremiah the prophet speaks, and the weeks’ goal is to seal up vision and prophet. The sitting reads 9:24’s phrase as the closing of a filing system — prophecy gets a verified fulfillment date, not retirement.

H8605.derivation: From palal, to judge or interpose: prayer — petition placed before the Judge.
H8605.gloss: prayer (1890: the book’s only full prayer opens here).

danielHits.gloss: I set my face… to seek by prayer
O our God, hear the prayer of thy servant

otherKjv.gloss: in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee
let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense

H8605.why: Chapter 9’s prayer is confession before it is request — Daniel judges himself before asking God to judge the calendar. Psalm 141 sets prayer beside the evening sacrifice; 9:21 shows the hour kept. The sitting uses 9:3 as the template: read the prophecy, pray the sin, then ask for the light.

H8469.derivation: From chanan, to bend or stoop in kindness: supplication — the entreaty of someone leaning on favor.
H8469.gloss: supplications (1890: asking from grace, not from claims).

danielHits.gloss: by prayer and supplications
and his supplications

otherKjv.gloss: The LORD hath received my supplication

H8469.why: The plural is deliberate: supplication is not one ask but a posture of asking. Daniel has covenant grounds (9:4) and still kneels as a beggar of mercy. The sitting holds grace and arithmetic together — the calendar is trusted because the Favor is real.

H6685.derivation: From tsuwm, to cover the mouth: a fast.
H6685.gloss: fasting (1890: the mouth closed so the prayer is heard).

danielHits.gloss: with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes

otherKjv.gloss: turn ye even to me… with fasting and with weeping
proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth

H6685.why: The fast answers the math: seventy years read, and the body joins the confession. Joel called for exactly this before judgment; Nineveh did it as a city. The sitting watches the prophet-to-Nineveh’s empire do prophet-work on itself.

H8242.derivation: A primitive root: sackcloth — the goat-hair garment of mourning.
H8242.gloss: sackcloth (1890: the uniform of grief worn by a statesman).

danielHits.gloss: with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes

otherKjv.gloss: Jacob… put sackcloth upon his loins
covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes

H8242.why: Jacob mourned a torn coat with sackcloth; Nineveh’s king wore it for a doomed city; Daniel wears it for a judged one. The sitting lets 9:3 stand as the reverse missionary moment — the capital’s most decorated exile dresses the empire’s sin as his own.

H1403.derivation: From H1398 geber (a strong man) and H410 El: “man/warrior of God.”
H1403.gloss: Gabriel (1890: the explaining angel; the same courier at the manger).

danielHits.gloss: Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision
the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning

otherKjv.gloss: I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God

H1403.why: One interpreter, two timelines: Gabriel explains the 2,300 (ch 8) and the seventy weeks (ch 9) — the sitting takes chapter 9 as chapter 8’s answer sheet, delivered by the same hand. Luke 1 sends the same name again: God’s strong man still does explaining.

H4503.derivation: From chanah, to apportion: a gift apportioned — the grain offering; the evening hour’s oblation.
H4503.gloss: oblation / offering (1890: the meal-gift; 9:21 keeps its hour, 9:27 names its end).

danielHits.gloss: about the time of the evening oblation
in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease

otherKjv.gloss: when any will offer a meat (grain) offering
Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering

H4503.why: Minchah is the ground’s gift — Cain’s word. In exile the evening minchah-hour still marks prayer (9:21); in 9:27 its end is dated to the week’s middle. The sitting puts the two together: when the true Offering is cut off (9:26), the shadow-gift loses its meaning — cessation as fulfillment.

H1697.derivation: From dabar, to arrange words: a word, matter, thing — speech as substance.
H1697.gloss: word / commandment (1890: the decree-word — creation by it, exile timed by it, restoration launched by it).

danielHits.gloss: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah
from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem

otherKjv.gloss: the word of the LORD came unto Abram in a vision
by the word of the LORD were the heavens made

H1697.why: Psalm 33:6 says worlds are made by this word; Daniel 9 times restoration by one — 457 B.C., Ezra 7. The sitting treats 9:25’s dabar as the starting gun: an imperial decree is Heaven’s word in drag, dated and counted.

H6695.derivation: From tsuq, to compress: distress — pressure, straits.
H6695.gloss: troublous (1890: “in troublous times” — the rebuilding runs under compression).

danielHits.gloss: the street shall be built again… even in troublous times

otherKjv.gloss: Trouble and anguish have taken hold on me

H6695.why: The clock starts under pressure, not in a golden age: Ezra 4-6 shows the builders a trowel in one hand and opposition in every other. The sitting notes the realism — prophecy dates are set inside politics, not above it.

H5057.derivation: From nagad, to front or stand out: a leader — one set before others.
H5057.gloss: prince / ruler (1890: three princes in three verses — keep them distinct).

danielHits.gloss: unto the Messiah the Prince
the people of the prince that shall come
the prince of the covenant

otherKjv.gloss: thou shalt anoint him to be captain (nagid) over my people
my servant David a prince among them

H5057.why: The anointed Prince cut off is not the Roman prince who destroys the city, nor the covenant-prince figure of 11:22 — grammar and dates keep them apart. The sitting’s method lesson: one word, three candidates, one context at a time.

H7858.derivation: From shataph, to gush: a flood — an overflowing torrent.
H7858.gloss: flood (1890: “the end thereof shall be with a flood” — armies as water).

danielHits.gloss: the end thereof shall be with a flood
the arms of a flood shall be swept away

otherKjv.gloss: with an overrunning flood he will make an utter end

H7858.why: Nahum used the word for Nineveh’s end; Daniel uses it for the city-desolation and the northern king’s arms. Floods do not negotiate — the sitting reads the figure as total, sudden, judged overflow.

H2782.derivation: A primitive root: to cut in, decide sharply — to determine by decree.
H2782.gloss: determined (1890: the sibling of H2852 chathak — two “determined” verbs in one prayer).

danielHits.gloss: unto the end of the war desolations are determined

otherKjv.gloss: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness

H2782.why: 9:24 cuts off the weeks (chathak); 9:26 cuts into the city (charats). Isaiah used the same verb for a decreed consumption. The sitting keeps the two cuts straight — one starts the 490, one levels the city — both decisions, both dated.

H1396.derivation: A primitive root: to be strong, prevail, strengthen.
H1396.gloss: confirm (1890: “he shall confirm the covenant” — cause-to-prevail, not merely sign).

danielHits.gloss: he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week

otherKjv.gloss: Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD

H1396.why: Gabar is strength applied. In 9:27 the covenant is made to prevail — by the Anointed One, in the middle of the week, where He is cut off but not for himself. The sitting reads the cross as the covenant’s reinforcement, not its suspension; futurism’s gap must erase this verb.

H2077.derivation: From zabach, to slaughter: a sacrifice — the blood-side of the altar.
H2077.gloss: sacrifice (1890: “cause the sacrifice to cease” — the animal clock stops).

danielHits.gloss: he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease

otherKjv.gloss: It is the sacrifice of the LORD’s passover
and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac

H2077.why: The passover established the slaughter-clock; 9:27 dates its stop — the week’s middle, the cross. Hebrews says the shadow ends when the substance bleeds. The sitting reads cessation as completion: the Lamb ends the lambs.

H8251.derivation: From shaqats, to be filthy: an abomination — especially an idol.
H8251.gloss: abomination (1890: the idol planted where God’s service stood).

danielHits.gloss: for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate
they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate
the abomination that maketh desolate

otherKjv.gloss: Ashtoreth… Chemosh the abomination of Moab
they have set their abominations in the house

H8251.why: Solomon’s foreign gods were called shiqquwts in God’s own house; Daniel’s horn places the same class of thing on the same ground. Jesus points at Daniel’s word in Matthew 24:15 as still future from His own day. The sitting tracks the word as a location marker: where the abomination stands, the sanctuary is being trespassed.

H5769.derivation: From alam, to hide: hidden time — eternity, forever, the long duration.
H5769.gloss: everlasting (1890: the age-word that outlives every metal).

danielHits.gloss: to bring in everlasting righteousness
some to everlasting life
shine as the stars for ever

otherKjv.gloss: the everlasting God
from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God

H5769.why: Olam is time seen from behind a curtain — duration God alone can see end to end. The 490 aims to bring in everlasting righteousness; 12:2-3 hands everlasting life and starlight to the wise. The sitting pairs it with Aramaic le'elmin (H5957): two languages, one forever.

H6664.derivation: From tsadaq (H6663): rightness, righteousness — the straightness of the court’s scale.
H6664.gloss: righteousness (1890: what the 490 brings IN — not what it leaves out).

danielHits.gloss: to bring in everlasting righteousness

otherKjv.gloss: righteousness and judgment are the habitation of his throne
my righteousness shall not be removed

H6664.why: The weeks end in a positive deposit: righteousness brought in, at the throne’s address. Rooted in 8:14’s nitsdaq, the sitting reads the whole arc as God putting things right on a calendar — the sanctuary, the city, the heart.

H2856.derivation: A primitive root: to seal — to close up with an authenticating mark.
H2856.gloss: seal (1890: 9:24 seals the vision; 12:4 seals the book — dated release).

danielHits.gloss: to seal up the vision and prophecy
and seal the book, even to the time of the end

otherKjv.gloss: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples
sealed with the king’s ring
