H2856.why: Sealing is not hiding; it is dating. The king’s ring made documents law for a set moment. The sitting reads 9:24 and 12:4 together: prophecy is certified, filed, and scheduled to speak at the time of the end — which is why knowledge increases then.

H4886.derivation: A primitive root: to smear, anoint — oil as ordination.
H4886.gloss: anoint (1890: the 490 ends in an anointing; the Anointed arrives at its 483rd year).

danielHits.gloss: to anoint the most Holy

otherKjv.gloss: thou shalt anoint him (the priest)
Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him (David)

H4886.why: Priests and kings were smeared into office; the weeks’ terminus is an anointing — and 9:25 has already timed the Messiah. The sitting lets 9:24-25 set each other: the anointed Most Holy and the Anointed Prince are one arithmetic with two headlines.

H5892.derivation: From uwr (to wake): a city — a waking, guarded place.
H5892.gloss: city (1890: the city rebuilt to a date and destroyed to a date).

danielHits.gloss: the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem — the city under the weeks
the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city

otherKjv.gloss: the wall was completed in fifty and two days

H5892.why: The same prophecy times her building and her burning. The sitting refuses to keep 9:26 for Babylon’s future only: the city fell in A.D. 70, on the prophecy’s own grammar — and the sanctuary verdicts of 8:14 keep running.

H426.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H433 elowahh: God — the court’s word for deity, true or false.
H426.gloss: God / god (1890: the same Aramaic word names the God of heaven and “the gods” of gold).

danielHits.gloss: there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets
our God whom we serve… we will not serve thy gods
the fourth is like bar-Elahin — a son of God
they praised the gods of gold and silver

otherKjv.gloss: prophesied… in the name of the God of Israel

H426.why: One word, two loyalties — context rules. 2:28 gives it to the Revealer; 3:5 gives it to an image; 3:25 hangs it on the fourth man; 5:4 watches it toasted in the stolen cups. The sitting uses elah as the book’s balance-scale: whichever god holds the word must hold the evidence.

H8065.gloss: heaven (1890: “the God of heaven” — the exiles’ name for God while the temple stands ruined).

danielHits.gloss: there is a God in heaven
the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom
the God of heaven shall set up a kingdom
under the whole heaven

otherKjv.gloss: the God of heaven

H8065.why: “God of heaven” is exile vocabulary — the temple is burned, so Heaven is the address. Twice in chapter 2 the phrase hands kingdoms out; 7:27 stretches the phrase over the whole sky. The sitting notes the irony: Babylon taught Daniel the name, and the name outlived Babylon.

H5094.derivation: (Aramaic) from a root meaning to shine: light.
H5094.gloss: light (1890: “the light dwelleth with him” — the court’s darkness answered).

danielHits.gloss: he knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him

H5094.why: Daniel 2:22 is a cosmology in one line: secrets live in darkness; light lives with God. Babylon’s guilds query darkness for hire; Heaven hosts the Light personally. The sitting lets 2:22 set the chapter’s terms — revelation is fellowship with the One in whom light lives, not the extraction of favors.

H1505.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1504 gazar, to cut: here “cut out” — quarry-language for a stone taken from a mountain.
H1505.gloss: cut out (1890: the stone is quarried, not manufactured).

danielHits.gloss: a stone was cut out without hands
the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands

H1505.why: To quarry is to separate by authority of the rock itself. The sitting loves the word’s texture: the kingdom of God is not assembled from the world’s metals; it is hewn out — and the mountain it comes from is a kingdom too (2:35, 44).

H3028.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3027 yad: hand — power, agency.
H3028.gloss: hand (1890: negated twice — “without hands”: not by human power).

danielHits.gloss: a stone was cut out without hands
cut out of the mountain without hands
he shall be broken without hand

H3028.why: Two negations, one doctrine. The stone arrives with no human agency; the horn falls with no human rescue. The sitting keeps the pair in view — everything God’s kingdom does is unassisted, and everything the horn trusts is unhelped in the end.

H2906.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6697 tsur: a mountain, cliff.
H2906.gloss: mountain (1890: the quarry-site of the stone — a kingdom on a kingdom).

danielHits.gloss: the stone… became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth
cut out of the mountain without hands

H2906.why: The stone comes out of a mountain and becomes one — kingdom from kingdom, not from parliaments. The sitting reads 2:35 and 2:45 as one sentence: God’s rule is cut from Heaven’s own range and lands as the range that fills the earth.

H4430.gloss: king (1890: “king of kings” — a title God lends and then collects).

danielHits.gloss: thou, O king, art a king of kings
I praise and honour the King of heaven

otherKjv.gloss: Artaxerxes, king of kings, unto Ezra

H4430.why: Nebuchadnezzar receives “king of kings” as a grant (2:37) and returns the title to its owner by chapter’s end (4:37): the King of heaven. Ezra’s Persian court used the same court-language. The sitting watches one syllable travel from flattery to worship.

H7981.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to a root meaning to dominate: to have dominion, bear rule.
H7981.gloss: bear rule (1890: the third kingdom’s verb — rule over all the earth).

danielHits.gloss: a third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth

H7981.why: Dominion is granted with geography attached. The sitting lets 2:39 set Greece’s scale before chapter 7-8 supply its wings and speed: the metal is brass, the verb is total rule, the evidence is Alexander.

H6966.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6965 qum: to arise, set up, establish — make to stand.
H6966.gloss: set up (1890: man sets up an image; God sets up a kingdom — one verb, two hands).

danielHits.gloss: the God of heaven shall set up a kingdom
Nebuchadnezzar… set it up (the image)
the golden image which thou hast set up

H6966.why: The same Aramaic verb in two paragraphs: the king stands up his gold statue on Dura, and God stands up an everlasting kingdom in the days of the divided feet. The sitting reads 3:1 against 2:44 like a caption: counterfeits get erected; the true kingdom gets established.

H2255.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2254 chabal, to ruin: destroy, hurt — ropes and ruin share the root.
H2255.gloss: destroyed / hurt (1890: what the stone-kingdom never is; what the lions’ mouths never did).

danielHits.gloss: a kingdom which shall never be destroyed
his angel… and have not hurt me

H2255.why: Chabal binds and wrecks. The book hangs two negations on it: the stone-kingdom shall never be destroyed (2:44), and Daniel is not hurt in the den (6:22). The sitting keeps both scenes on one rail — untouched is a category Heaven grants by verdict, not by circumstance.

H5957.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5769 owlam: remote time — eternity; often adverbially, for ever.
H5957.gloss: for ever / everlasting (1890: the forever-word handed to the Son of man).

danielHits.gloss: it shall stand for ever
his dominion is an everlasting dominion
everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away
possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever

H5957.why: Le'elmin is owlam in the court’s tongue. The sitting tracks the word’s ownership: the God of heaven sets up a forever-kingdom (2:44), the Son of man receives it (7:14), the saints inherit with Him (7:18) — and the gold king confesses it from the grass (4:34).

H6399.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6398 palach: to serve or worship — minister, serve.
H6399.gloss: serve (1890: the whole trial of chapter 3 in one verb — whom will you serve?).

danielHits.gloss: these men… serve not thy gods
our God whom we serve… we will not serve thy gods
that they might not serve nor worship any god
thy God whom thou servest continually
all people… should serve him
all dominions shall serve and obey him

otherKjv.gloss: the servants (pelache) of the house of God

H6399.why: Chapter 3 is a jurisdiction fight over one verb. Babylon demands pelach; the three refuse it for any god but theirs; the record’s ending hands the same verb to the Son of man (7:14) and to every dominion under Him (7:27). The sitting reads 3:18 and 7:27 as the book’s two answers to one question.

H5457.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5456 cagad: to bow down, worship — prostrate oneself.
H5457.gloss: worship (1890: the body-language of the Dura decree).

danielHits.gloss: fall down and worship the golden image
nor worship the golden image
yielded their bodies that they might not serve nor worship any god

H5457.why: Segid is the knee, not the creed: Babylon asks for posture first. The three will not give the knee (3:18) — and chapter 2 already showed what their posture costs God nothing to overturn. The sitting pairs 3:5 with 3:18: worship is a jurisdiction, and jurisdiction is what the stone-kingdom settles.

H7804.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5800 azab, to leave free: to deliver, rescue — release from custody.
H7804.gloss: deliver (1890: the mocker’s word becomes the martyr’s confession).

danielHits.gloss: who is that God that shall deliver you?
our God… is able to deliver us
he sent his angel, and delivered his servants
thy God whom thou servest continually will he deliver thee?
able to deliver you from the lions?

H7804.why: The verb travels: Nebuchadnezzar sneers it (3:15), the three answer it (3:17), fire proves it (3:28), and Darius ends chapter 6 asking it in wonder (6:20). The sitting hears the same word change sides — from taunt to testimony.

H4398.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4397 mal'ak: a messenger — angel.
H4398.gloss: angel (1890: Heaven’s envoy inside the furnace and inside the den).

danielHits.gloss: he sent his angel, and delivered his servants
my God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths

H4398.why: Two sealed pits, two visitors: the furnace and the den both get an angel. The Hebrew sibling malak (H4397) runs from Jacob’s ladder to Malachi’s promise. The sitting notes what the angels do — they shut mouths and walk in fire; rescue is official business.

H8540.derivation: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H8539 tamah (to be astonished): a wonder, a miracle.
H8540.gloss: wonders (1890: the signs Gentile kings end up confessing).

danielHits.gloss: I thought it good to shew the signs and wonders
he worketh signs and wonders in heaven and in earth

H8540.why: Nebuchadnezzar opens his personal testimony with them (4:2); Darius closes the lions’ night with them (6:27). Two Gentile kings, both once God’s critics, both end up witnessing timhen. The sitting uses the word as chapter markers: the empire keeps being surprised.

H6136.derivation: (Aramaic) from aqar (to uproot): a stock, stump — what remains after felling.
H6136.gloss: stump (1890: the mercy inside the judgment — the kingdom cut down, not annihilated).

danielHits.gloss: leave the stump of his roots in the earth
the stump of the tree roots
whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the tree roots

H6136.why: The stump is God’s sentence with a survival clause: the kingdom is cut down for seven times, but the roots are kept in the earth, banded with iron and brass. The sitting reads the stump against 2:44 — earthly kingdoms get trimmed; the stone-kingdom is the one that cannot be cut.

H3825.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3824 lebab: the heart — the enclosed inner man.
H3825.gloss: heart (1890: a beast’s heart for the gold king; a man’s heart given back to the lion).

danielHits.gloss: let his heart be changed from man’s, and let a beast’s heart be given unto him
his heart was made like the beasts
a man’s heart was given to it

H3825.why: Chapter 7:4’s lion loses wings and gains a man’s heart — chapter 4 is that verse lived out in real time. The sitting joins lebab across the two languages (Hebrew lebab at 1:8, Aramaic lebab here): purposing hearts and beast-hearts are the book’s two states of man.

H2417.derivation: (Aramaic) from chaya' (H2418 family): alive — living, life.
H2417.gloss: living (1890: “him that liveth for ever” — the Living One beside dead gold).

danielHits.gloss: I blessed the most High, and… him that liveth for ever
O Daniel, servant of the living God
He is the living God, and stedfast for ever

H2417.why: Chapter 4-6 build a confession out of a word: the Living One versus the metal-and-stone gods of 5:4 that cannot see, hear, or know. The sitting lets 4:34’s recovered king say it first, and Darius’s decree say it louder. Hebrew chay (H2416) swears the book’s final oath (12:7).

H5943.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5942 illiy: the high one — most high.
H5943.gloss: most High (1890: the title above every “king of kings”).

danielHits.gloss: the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men
till thou know that the most High ruleth
I blessed the most High

H5943.why: Chapter 4 is a lesson plan with one learning objective: know that the most High rules (4:25, said to the king directly). The sitting notes the grammar — the most High rules IN the kingdom of men; supervision is the doctrine, not distance. Chapter 7’s elyownin (H5946) is the sibling title over the saints.

H6922.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6918 qadowsh: holy — the holy one, the saint.
H6922.gloss: holy one / saint (1890: heaven’s sentinels and God’s persecuted people share one word).

danielHits.gloss: a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven
the decree of the watchers… the word of the holy ones
the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom
he shall wear out the saints of the most High

H6922.why: The same qaddiysh describes the sentinels who sentence the gold king and the people the little horn wears out. The sitting’s lesson: the saints inherit what the holy ones decree — jurisdiction belongs to the set-apart, whatever the court of Babylon says.

H7985.derivation: (Aramaic) from shelat (H7981): dominion — ruling authority as a possession.
H7985.gloss: dominion (1890: the contested prize of chapters 4-7).

danielHits.gloss: his dominion is an everlasting dominion
their dominion was taken away
the kingdom and dominion… given to the people of the saints

H7985.why: Dominion is transferable by Heaven’s audit: the beasts lose theirs (7:12), the Son of man receives it (7:14), the saints inherit it (7:27), and the gold king confesses its real owner (4:34). The sitting lets sholtan be the ledger-word of the whole book.

H5491.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5486 cuwph: an end — the boundary of a thing.
H5491.gloss: end (1890: God’s dominion runs to it; the horn’s is taken to it).

danielHits.gloss: his dominion shall be even unto the end
they shall take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it unto the end

H5491.why: Two ends in two chapters: God’s dominion reaches the end (6:26); the little horn’s dominion is removed to the end (7:26). The sitting sets them side by side — the same horizon, opposite verdicts.

H1467.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1344 gevah: pride, haughtiness — swelling.
H1467.gloss: pride (1890: chapter 4’s final diagnosis, from the recovered patient).

danielHits.gloss: those that walk in pride he is able to abase

H1467.why: The book’s most relieved sentence: written by the man who ate grass. Pride is walkable — a daily gait, not one outburst — and Heaven can abase it at will. The sitting ends chapter 4 on gevah because chapter 5’s feast (5:22-23) shows the next generation refusing to learn it.

H1113.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1095 Beltsha'tstsar: “Bel, protect the king.”
H1113.gloss: Belshazzar (1890: the Bel-name that blasphemes with the stolen cups).

danielHits.gloss: Belshazzar the king made a feast… and drank in the vessels
thou… hast not humbled thine heart

H1113.why: Belshazzar and Belteshazzar share a god and a question: whose king does Bel protect? The night of the wall answers — the vessels count the feast, the feast counts the kingdom, and the protector-god protects nothing. The sitting notes Daniel’s charge (5:22): he knew chapter 4’s lesson and refused it.

H1965.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1964 heykal: a palace or temple — the great-house.
H1965.gloss: temple / palace (1890: the same word serves the palace and the sanctuary — chapter 5 blurs them on purpose).

danielHits.gloss: the golden vessels taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem

H1965.why: Heykal means great house — king’s palace or God’s temple. Belshazzar’s feast makes the two one room: sanctuary vessels at a palace party. The sitting reads the blurring as the crime: what was set apart is being used as furniture.

H636.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6086 ets: wood, timber.
H636.gloss: wood (1890: the dead fifth substance in the god-list).

danielHits.gloss: gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone
the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone

H636.why: The statue’s four metals return as a god-list, padded with wood and stone. Two materials that neither see, hear, nor know (5:23) — and the feast praises them anyway. The sitting uses the inventory as chapter 5’s charge sheet: worship assigned to lumber.

H4756.derivation: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to mara' (to be master): a lord, master.
H4756.gloss: Lord (1890: “the Lord of heaven” — the title Belshazzar lifts himself against).

danielHits.gloss: thou hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven

otherKjv.gloss: unto Ezra the priest, a scribe of the law of the God of heaven — from a court that used the same court-language

H4756.why: Flattery and treason use the same vocabulary: kings collect “my lord the king” all through the book (4:19). The sitting marks 5:23 because the charge is precise — against the Lord (mare') of heaven, with the temple cups in hand.

H5396.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5397 neshamah: vital breath — the loaned spark of life.
H5396.gloss: breath (1890: “in whose hand thy breath is” — the audit’s hidden clause).

danielHits.gloss: the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified

H5396.why: Genesis 2:7’s breath belongs to God; Daniel says Belshazzar’s next breath is still in that hand — while he drinks from God’s cups. The sitting pairs 5:23 with 5:25-28: the writing does not announce a new judgment; it reads out an old one against a man living on borrowed air.

H1868.derivation: (Aramaic) of Persian origin: Darius — “holder of the scepter/good.”
H1868.gloss: Darius (1890: the Mede who receives the kingdom on the feast-night).

danielHits.gloss: Darius the Median took the kingdom
it pleased Darius to set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes

H1868.why: “Took the kingdom” is receive-language — qabbel — a transfer without a battle on the night the wall said “divided.” The sitting lets 5:31 answer 5:28 in real time: Peres was not a metaphor; it was Tuesday.

H4077.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4074 Maday: a Mede — the land of Media.
H4077.gloss: the Median (1890: the bear’s first arm arrives on schedule).

danielHits.gloss: Darius the Median took the kingdom
the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not

H4077.why: Maday steps into chapter 5 the way the bear was raised on one side (7:5) — Media visible, Persia rising. The sitting lets 5:31 verify 2:39: the silver is now on the throne, and the unchangeable law of 6:8 belongs to the transfer.

H7308.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7307 ruwach: wind, spirit, breath.
H7308.gloss: spirit (1890: the same word makes Daniel excellent and makes him distressed).

danielHits.gloss: an excellent spirit was found in him
my spirit was troubled in the midst of my body

H7308.why: One word, two states: the spirit that makes a statesman excel (6:3) and the spirit that reels when prophecy turns carnivorous (7:15). The sitting holds both — the gift does not cancel the burden; Hebrew ruach (H7307) says the same across the language line.

H1358.derivation: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to guwb (to dig): a pit — a den cut for beasts.
H1358.gloss: den (1890: the pit dug for lions, hosting a prayer meeting).

danielHits.gloss: cast into the den of lions
they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions

H1358.why: A dug pit with a stone over its mouth (6:17) — the sitting cannot miss the echo of a garden tomb. The den built to end Daniel becomes the place where the living God is confessed by an empire (6:26-27). The pit is the pulpit.

H6606.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6607 pethach: an opening — door, window.
H6606.gloss: windows (1890: openness as witness — prayer with the shutters up).

danielHits.gloss: his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem

H6606.why: The decree banned prayer; Daniel answered with architecture — windows open, facing a city in ruins. The sitting reads the openings as testimony: secrecy was available and refused. What follows (the den, the angel, the decree of 6:26) all issues from a window.

H3390.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3389 Yerushalaim: Jerusalem — the city of peace.
H3390.gloss: Jerusalem (1890: the direction of banned prayer).

danielHits.gloss: his windows open… toward Jerusalem

H3390.why: Solomon’s dedication asked that prayers toward this city be heard even in exile (1 Kings 8:48). Daniel’s window assumes the promise still works with the temple in ashes. The sitting keeps the compass-point: chapter 9’s calendar and chapter 6’s courage both aim at Jerusalem.

H6739.derivation: (Aramaic) probably from tsela' in the sense of bowing: to pray — to bend low.
H6739.gloss: pray (1890: the posture is the definition).

danielHits.gloss: he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed
he kneeled… and prayed, and gave thanks, as he did aforetime

H6739.why: Kneeling is baked into the verb. Daniel’s practice was public, habitual, and old (“as he did aforetime”) — the sitting notes that courage here is not a new decision but a kept habit meeting a new decree.

H8411.derivation: (Aramaic) from duwr in the sense of enduring: permanence — constantly, continually, the same round returning.
H8411.gloss: continually (1890: the adverb of Daniel’s habit — and the accuser’s evidence).

danielHits.gloss: thy God whom thou servest continually
the God whom thou servest continually

H8411.why: Tadir is a rhythm that keeps returning — Daniel’s three-times-a-day round (6:10, with zeman, H2166). Compare H8548 tamid, the Hebrew word for the continual daily service: both point to a standing, unbroken ministry. The sitting lets the adverb convict an empire: what Darius says mournfully, the satraps said maliciously.

H3764.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3678 kisse': a throne — the judicial seat.
H3764.gloss: throne (1890: thrones plural are “placed” before the court convenes).

danielHits.gloss: thrones were cast down (set in place), and the Ancient of days did sit

H3764.why: A court needs a bench: the Aramaic says seats were positioned — procedural, not stormy. The sitting contrasts 7:9’s set thrones with the beasts’ thrown-down thrones; judgment is furniture before it is fire.

H5135.derivation: (Aramaic) from an unused root meaning to shine: fire.
H5135.gloss: fire (1890: the flame that tested the three also flows before the Judge).

danielHits.gloss: the burning fiery furnace
his throne was like the fiery flame
the fiery stream issued and came forth from before him

H5135.why: Same fire, two roles: in chapter 3 it tests the faithful and escorts a fourth man; in chapter 7 it pours from the Ancient of days as judicial output. The sitting joins the scenes — the God who walked in the furnace is the God whose river of fire opens the books.

H5609.derivation: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5608 caphar: a book, roll — a counted writing.
H5609.gloss: books (1890: the court’s records opened before judgment is executed).

danielHits.gloss: the judgment was set, and the books were opened

H5609.why: Courts keep records; opened books mean reviewed lives. The sitting links 7:10 to 12:1’s book of the delivered and to Daniel’s own “seal the book” (12:4): Heaven’s filings are real, dated, and decisive.

H6050.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6051 anan: a cloud — the thunderhead-chariot.
H6050.gloss: clouds (1890: the Son of man arrives on the throne-chariot).

danielHits.gloss: one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven

otherKjv.gloss: who maketh the clouds his chariot

H6050.why: Psalm 104 says clouds are God’s chariot; Daniel sees a man on them. Jesus claims the verse at His trial (“hereafter shall ye see the Son of man… coming in the clouds”). The sitting reads 7:13 as deity-credentials in cloud form — and as the Second Coming’s standard picture.

H5403.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5404 nesher: an eagle — the bird of speed and spoil.
H5403.gloss: eagle (1890: the winged lion — Babylon’s real gate-statues).

danielHits.gloss: the first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings

otherKjv.gloss: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle

H5403.why: Winged lions stood at Babylon’s gates; the archaeology is Daniel’s footnotes. Jeremiah said the eagle would be plucked from its nest; Daniel watches the wings plucked and a man’s heart given — chapter 4 in beast-language. The sitting lets the statue confirm the symbol.

H1080.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1086 balah (to wear away): to wear out — attrition of the saints.
H1080.gloss: wear out (1890: persecution as slow grinding, not one decree).

danielHits.gloss: he shall wear out the saints of the most High

H1080.why: A mental-grind verb: the horn’s war is attrition — lawsuits, fatigue, eras of pressure. The sitting contrasts it with 7:27’s verdict: what is worn out by a policy is inherited by a people; the grinding has a stop-date.

H4484.derivation: (Aramaic) passive participle of H4483 menah: numbered. The same letters spell the mina — the standard silver weight of the empire.
H4484.gloss: MENE — numbered (1890: the word on the wall doubles as the coin-weight Babylon lived by).

danielHits.gloss: MENE, MENE — the writing the king could read but not answer
This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE

otherKjv.gloss: after their ability they gave unto the treasure of the work — mina-weights of gold

H4484.why: The hand writes a word every money-changer knows: the mina. Babylon’s wealth is audited on its own scales. The sitting reads the pun as the sentence — what you counted in minas is now counted out; the weighed kingdom is spent.

H2166.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2165 zeman: an appointed time — a fixed moment.
H2166.gloss: time (1890: God changes them (2:21); Daniel keeps them (6:10); the horn plans to change them (7:25)).

danielHits.gloss: he changeth the times and the seasons
he kneeled… three times a day
think to change times and laws

H2166.why: Three chapters, one word, one war. God changes the times (2:21) — the sitting’s sovereignty text; Daniel keeps his times (6:10) — the discipleship text; the little horn intends to change them (7:25) — the agenda text. The timetable is the battlefield.

H5946.derivation: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5945 elyown: the Supreme — Most High.
H5946.gloss: most High (1890: the title over the saints’ inheritance — the horn’s target).

danielHits.gloss: the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom
he shall speak great words against the most High
the people of the saints of the most High

H5946.why: Chapter 7’s Most High owns the kingdom the horn covets: he speaks against Him (7:25) and wears out His people, and the court answers with inheritance for the saints (7:27). The sitting pairs illay (H5943, ch. 4) with elyownin — one throne, two languages, zero vacancies.

H3800.derivation: From katham (to carve or mark): gold as originally mined — ore-pure, carved out.
H3800.gloss: fine gold (1890: “fine gold of Uphaz” — metal straight from the vein).

danielHits.gloss: a certain man… whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz

otherKjv.gloss: more to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold
the topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it

H3800.why: Kethem is pre-minted purity — no refining needed, no alloy. The figure of 10:5-6 wears what Scripture uses to grade truth itself (Ps 19:10). The sitting lets the clothing speak: this is the Presence, not a courtier — and chapter 9’sPrince of prayer is about to be strengthened by Him.

H8658.derivation: Probably of foreign derivation (compare Tarshish): a gem — the beryl, perhaps the chrysolite.

danielHits.gloss: his body also was like the beryl

otherKjv.gloss: the fourth row, a beryl in the high priest’s breastplate
the colour of a beryl; and the four had one likeness

H8658.why: Tarshiysh glints in three places: Aaron’s breastplate, Ezekiel’s wheels, Daniel’s visitor. The sitting reads the wardrobe as credentials — sanctuary-glint on the man by the river, the same family of fire as chapter 7’s throne.

H1300.derivation: From baraq (to lighten): lightning — a flash, a gleaming blade.
H1300.gloss: lightning (1890: Sinai-glint on the messenger’s face).

danielHits.gloss: his face as the appearance of lightning

otherKjv.gloss: thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount

H1300.why: Faces shone after Sinai because they had been near glory; this face is glory (10:6). The sitting ties 10:5-6 to 7:9-10 and Revelation 1 — one vocabulary of throne-visitations. The messenger leaves Daniel strengthless (10:8); holiness weighs.

H3940.derivation: From an unused root meaning to shine: a torch, lamp — flame carried by hand.
H3940.gloss: lamps (1890: “eyes as lamps of fire” — the Searcher’s gaze).

danielHits.gloss: his eyes as lamps of fire

otherKjv.gloss: the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings
the torches in the left hand of Gideon’s three hundred

H3940.why: Torches search out darkness; these eyes are torches of fire. The sitting hears Daniel 10 answering Daniel 2:22 — the One in whom light dwells has come to the Tigris, and His eyes keep the books. Revelation 1:14 keeps the picture.

H5178.derivation: For nechuwshah: copper, bronze — the judgment-metal of the altar.

danielHits.gloss: his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass

otherKjv.gloss: Moses made a serpent of brass
Hiram… filled with wisdom… to work all works in brass

H5178.why: Bronze bore the altar and the serpent-lifted-up. The Aramaic brass of 2:32 (H5174) is a kingdom; this burnished bronze is a body — judgment and wisdom in one figure. The sitting keeps the metals vocabularies separate: statue-metals, sanctuary-metals.

H1995.derivation: From hamah (to murmur, roar): a noise, tumult — the sound of a crowd.
H1995.gloss: multitude (1890: “the voice of a multitude” — throne-room sound).

danielHits.gloss: the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude

otherKjv.gloss: the noise of a multitude in the mountains

H1995.why: Daniel stands alone by a river and hears a crowd — heaven is never thinly attended (7:10’s thousands). The sitting lets 10:6’s sound belong to the same audio-file as Revelation 1:15’s many waters: the Lord speaks with the weight of hosts.

H6031.derivation: A primitive root: to depress, afflict, humble — and so, to answer (the bowed reply).
H6031.gloss: chasten (1890: “to chasten thyself” — the Day of Atonement verb).

danielHits.gloss: thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God

otherKjv.gloss: ye shall afflict your souls… a sabbath of rest unto the Lord
Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows

H6031.why: Anah is the word Leviticus 23 assigns to the Day of Atonement (“afflict your souls”) and Isaiah 53 gives to the Servant. Daniel’s three-week humbling (10:2-3) runs on atonement-grammar. The sitting reads 10:12 as the verse’s hinge: understanding was heard because humility was offered.

H6539.derivation: Of foreign origin: Persia — the land that inherits the silver.
H6539.gloss: Persia (1890: the named power behind the ram and the bear).

danielHits.gloss: the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me
there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia

otherKjv.gloss: Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD might be fulfilled
Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus

H6539.why: Isaiah named Persia’s shepherd before Persia had a throne-room; Daniel shows the same empire hosting a hostile prince (10:13). The sitting keeps the双层 reality: kings on maps, princes behind them — history and the unseen war in one chapter.

H7223.derivation: From ri'shah: first — in place, time, or rank.
H7223.gloss: chief (1890: Michael, “one of the chief princes” — ranked, not rival).

danielHits.gloss: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me

otherKjv.gloss: I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God

H7223.why: Michael is first among princes — a rank inside a hierarchy. Isaiah’s “First” is YHWH alone. The sitting holds the distinction firmly: Michael the great prince (12:1) is the greatest envoy, not a second god; the book’s throne-room has exactly one occupant on the bench.

H319.derivation: From achar (after): the after-part — the end, the latter days, posterity.
H319.gloss: latter days (1890: “in the latter days” — the dated horizon of 10:14).

danielHits.gloss: what shall befall thy people in the latter days

otherKjv.gloss: that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days
I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days

H319.why: Jacob blessed his sons with acharith-yamim; Balaam used it for Israel’s future; Gabriel uses it for Daniel’s people. The phrase is a genre marker: dated futures for covenant people, not vague beyonds. The sitting lets 10:14 organize chapters 11-12 before they are read.

H3791.derivation: (Aramaic) from H3789 kathab: a writing, record — an Aramaic-form word standing in the Hebrew verse 10:21, as court-loan language for Heaven’s own docket.
H3791.gloss: scripture (1890: “the scripture of truth” — the war’s written docket).

danielHits.gloss: I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth

otherKjv.gloss: the letter… written in the Syrian tongue

H3791.why: Before chapter 11’s newspapers, Heaven has a filing cabinet: the writing of truth. Kings rise and fall as entries, not surprises. The sitting reads 10:21 as the license for historicism — the chain of 11:1-45 is recorded history, not allegory.

H3120.derivation: Probably from the same as yayin (effervescing): Javan — the Ionians, Greece; Japheth’s son in Genesis 10.
H3120.gloss: Grecia (1890: Greece by its Genesis name — on the map before it mattered).

danielHits.gloss: the rough goat is the king of Grecia
the prince of Grecia shall come
the fourth shall be far richer… and shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia

otherKjv.gloss: the sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog… and Javan
thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Javan

H3120.why: Yavan sat in the table of nations for two millennia before Alexander sprinted east. The sitting uses the name to connect 8:21’s goat, 10:20’s prince, and 11:2’s kingdom — one realm, one row in Genesis 10, no confusion of powers.

H1368.derivation: Intensive from geber: mighty — a warrior, champion.
H1368.gloss: mighty (1890: “a mighty king” — Alexander at full sprint).

danielHits.gloss: a mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great dominion

otherKjv.gloss: his name shall be called… The mighty God (El Gibbor)
Nimrod: he was a mighty hunter before the LORD

H1368.why: Gibbor crowns Nimrod’s empire-building and Isaiah’s God-with-us. Daniel 11:3’s mighty king conquers swiftly and shatters “not in his anger” (11:4). The sitting contrasts the two gibbors: the one who rules by dominance dies young; El Gibbor receives an everlasting dominion (7:14).

H5045.derivation: From an unused root meaning to be parched: the south — the dry Negeb district.
H5045.gloss: south (1890: “the king of the south” — Ptolemies, geography made prophetic).

danielHits.gloss: the king of the south shall be strong
the king of the south push at him

H5045.why: The word is desert — the parched quarter. Daniel 11’s chessboard runs north (H6828) and south between the Seleucids and Ptolemies, and 11:40-45 brings the drama to the glorious land. The sitting keeps the compass literal: prophecy writes geography.

H6828.derivation: From tsaphan (to hide): the hidden, dark quarter — the north.
H6828.gloss: north (1890: “the king of the north” — the Seleucid line).

danielHits.gloss: the king of the north shall come
the king of the north shall come against him like a whirlwind

otherKjv.gloss: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north

H6828.why: The north is the hidden side — where Assyria and Babylon attacked Israel, and where Lucifer plotted his throne. Daniel 11’s northern king inherits the direction’s whole biography. The sitting notes 11:45’s ending: he comes to his end “with none to help him” — the dark quarter runs out of map.

H2490.derivation: A primitive root: to bore, wound — hence to profane; to treat as common.
H2490.gloss: pollute (1890: “they shall pollute the sanctuary” — blur the holy and the common).

danielHits.gloss: they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength

otherKjv.gloss: take the name of the LORD thy God in vain
her priests have violated my law… and have put no difference between the holy and profane

H2490.why: Chalal is the blur — treating set-apart things as common. Ezekiel blamed priests for it; Daniel’s horn polices it into policy; the abomination follows the blur. The sitting reads 11:31 as the mechanism: first profanation, then placement (H8251), then desolation (H8074).

H7522.derivation: From ratsah (to be pleased): delight, goodwill — will as pleasure.
H7522.gloss: will (1890: “according to his will” — the willful king’s government of desire).

danielHits.gloss: the king shall do according to his will

otherKjv.gloss: I delight to do thy will, O my God
none should compel… according to every man’s pleasure

H7522.why: Two governments of will: the king who does his own pleasure (11:36) and the Servant whose delight was God’s (Ps 40:8). The sitting sets them over against each other — prophecy’s self-worshipper is the exact negative of the covenant’s Servant, and 11:45’s end shows whose pleasure held.

H1419.derivation: From gadal (to grow great): great — in size, age, or importance.
H1419.gloss: great (1890: “that great prince which standeth” — Michael’s greatness is his standing).

danielHits.gloss: Michael… the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people

otherKjv.gloss: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised

H1419.why: Greatness in Daniel 12 is posture: the prince stands for the people. Then comes the trouble that is great without peer. The sitting reads 12:1 in order — standing, trouble, book, deliverance — sequence is doctrine.

H4422.derivation: A primitive root: to be smooth — to slip away, escape; causatively, to deliver.

danielHits.gloss: at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book

otherKjv.gloss: Escape for thy life (Lot)
the seed of the righteous shall be delivered

H4422.why: Malat is Lot’s verb — running out of a doomed city. The deliverance of 12:1 is an escape bounded by a register: “every one found written in the book.” The sitting joins it to 7:25-27 — the worn-out saints are the escaped ones; both lists are Heaven’s.

H3789.derivation: A primitive root: to grave, inscribe, write.
H3789.gloss: written (1890: the register precedes the rescue).

danielHits.gloss: every one that shall be found written in the book

otherKjv.gloss: blot me… out of thy book which thou hast written
written among the living in Jerusalem

H3789.why: Moses offered to be blotted out of a book already written; Isaiah promises the living are registered in Jerusalem. Daniel 12:1 opens the same register before the trouble starts. The sitting lets 12:1 define the delivered: not the strong, the written.

H7549.derivation: From raqa' (to beat out, spread thin): an expanse — the hammered-out dome of the sky.
H7549.gloss: firmament (1890: creation’s ceiling; the wise shine with its brightness).

danielHits.gloss: shine as the brightness of the firmament

otherKjv.gloss: God called the firmament Heaven
the likeness of a firmament, as the colour of the terrible crystal

H7549.why: The firmament is day-two’s masterpiece — the spread sky over every living thing. Daniel’s wise shine with its own brightness, not a borrowed lamp. The sitting lets 12:3 hand creation-language to the resurrection classroom: the teachers become sky.

H3556.derivation: Probably from kabbown or kavah (to roll or blaze): a star — a rolling or blazing light.
H3556.gloss: stars (1890: Abraham’s promise-image; Balaam’s Star out of Jacob).

danielHits.gloss: they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever

otherKjv.gloss: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars
There shall come a Star out of Jacob

H3556.why: God promised Abraham star-seed and Balaam announced a star-king. Daniel 12:3 completes the image: the wise who turn many to righteousness become the stars — the promise’s shine passing to teachers. The sitting ends the book on glory given to the faithful.

H7751.derivation: A primitive root: to push forth, lash (the sea with oars) — hence to row, travel, run to and fro.
H7751.gloss: run to and fro (1890: the sealing’s expiration sign).

danielHits.gloss: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased

otherKjv.gloss: they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the LORD
going to and fro in the earth

H7751.why: Amos promised a famine of hearing with people running for the word; Job 1 shows the Adversary patrolling the same verb. Daniel 12 dates the reversal — the sealed book opens and knowledge increases. The sitting reads the running as the age of the opened prophecy: travel, printing, and the worldwide search.

H4150.derivation: From ya'ad (to appoint): an appointment — fixed time, festival, the meeting-place itself.
H4150.gloss: time (1890: the feast-word — 12:7’s formula uses God’s appointment vocabulary).

danielHits.gloss: it shall be for a time, times, and an half
from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away

otherKjv.gloss: concerning the feasts of the LORD — the appointed times
for seasons (mo'edim) — days and years

H4150.why: Mo'ed is the calendar of the sanctuary — Genesis 1 set the clock, Leviticus 23 filled it with feasts. Where 7:25 said the horn would change iddan-times (the court word), 12:7 swears the formula in mo'ed — God’s appointments. The sitting lets the vocabulary settle the argument: appointments cannot be amended by a horn.

H5310.derivation: A primitive root: to dash to pieces, scatter.
H5310.gloss: scatter (1890: “to scatter the power of the holy people” — shattering on a clock).

danielHits.gloss: when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people

otherKjv.gloss: the earth is utterly broken down
I will dash them one against another

H5310.why: The oath of 12:7 locks a shattering to a schedule: the holy people’s power is scattered for a time, times, and a half — not forever. Isaiah used naphats for earth’s own breaking. The sitting reads the scatter as the depth of the 1260-era and 12:1’s trouble — real, measured, and then reversed.

H2416.derivation: From chayah: alive — living, fresh, strong.
H2416.gloss: living (1890: the Hebrew twin of Aramaic chay — the oath’s basis).

danielHits.gloss: sware by him that liveth for ever

otherKjv.gloss: who is there of all flesh, that hath heard the voice of the living God
my heart and my flesh crieth out for the living God

H2416.why: The man in linen swears by the Living One — Hebrew chay at the oath, Aramaic chay (H2417) in the furnace-and-den confessions. The sitting lets 12:7 seal 7:25’s formula with the strongest basis a Hebrew oath can have: the Life that does not end.

H5117.derivation: A primitive root: to rest — settle down (the ark “rested,” God “rested” the seventh day).
H5117.gloss: rest (1890: Daniel’s last gift — the ark-word for finished work).

danielHits.gloss: Go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot

otherKjv.gloss: the ark rested in the seventh month
the LORD rested the seventh day

H5117.why: Nuwach is Noah’s verb and God’s sabbath verb — rest after passage, rest after work. Daniel is told to stop counting and wait; the flood passes over him as it did the ark. The sitting ends where the book ends: rest, then the lot — the assigned place at the end of the days.

H3784.derivation: A primitive root: to whisper a spell — to enchant, practise magic (the sorcerer’s verb).
H3784.gloss: sorcerers (1890: the spell-whisperers; a capital crime under the law — Ex 22:18).

danielHits.gloss: the sorcerers summoned with the magicians and astrologers

otherKjv.gloss: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live
against the sorcerers… saith the LORD of hosts

H3784.why: The law of Daniel’s God sentenced this craft to death; the court of Babylon staffs itself with it. The sitting uses 2:2 as the roster of guild-science — magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, Chaldeans — every class present, every class silent (2:10-11).

H5245.derivation: Corresponding to H5246: leopard, spotted and swift.
H5245.gloss: leopard (1890: Greece; four wings, then four heads).

danielHits.gloss: a leopard… four wings… four heads; dominion was given to it

otherKjv.gloss: the he-goat touches not the ground; the great horn breaks; four stand up
the goat is Grecia; four kingdoms out of the nation
their horses shall be swifter than the leopards

H5245.why: Four wings are Alexander’s speed; four heads are the Diadochi. Chapter 8 names the people. The sitting will not stop the third kingdom at one man’s life.

H825.derivation: From an unused root (probably meaning to lisp, i.e. to practice enchantment): a conjurer — the astrologer’s word in 1:20 and 2:2 (the Aramaic-form H826 ashshaph carries the same guild in 2:10; 4:6; 5:7, 11, 15).
H825.gloss: astrologers (1890: the enchanters’ caste — KJV’s word in the academy scene).

danielHits.gloss: the king found the Hebrew youth ten times better than all the astrologers
the astrologers summoned with the magicians, sorcerers, and Chaldeans

H825.why: One guild, two word-forms: the spell-whisperers Babylon hires by the roomful (2:2) are the same caste the Hebrew boys outrank tenfold (1:20) — without ever joining it. The sitting reads the academy scene as science without revelation: every class summoned, every class silent (2:10-11).

H3027.derivation: A primitive word: a hand (the open hand — power, means, direction; distinct from kaph, the closed hand).
H3027.gloss: hand (1890: agency, power — here negated: “broken without hand”).

danielHits.gloss: the horn that stood against the Prince of princes shall be broken without hand

otherKjv.gloss: by strength of hand the LORD brought you out
In his hand are the deep places of the earth

H3027.why: Two languages, one doctrine: the stone is cut without hands (2:34, Aramaic yedeyin, H3028) and the horn is broken without hand (8:25, Hebrew yad, H3027). What God does, He does unassisted; what the horn trusts, it loses unhelped. The sitting keeps the pair as one sentence spread across the book.
